 10.0   Deliverability Study


10.1   The Transmission Provider shall perform a Deliverability Study for the Summer Season
       and a Deliverability Study for the Winter Season every year. There will be a separate
       Deliverability Study each season for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and the SPP
       West Balancing Authority Area. The Deliverability Study for the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area will study the following: (1)
       whether a Resource is deliverable to load located within the same SPP Balancing
       Authority Area; and (2) whether the Resource is deliverable to load located in the SPP
       Balancing Authority Area where the Resource is not located. Each Deliverability Study
       will evaluate each Resource registered in the Integrated Marketplace to determine the
       Deliverable Capacity each Resource has to load located within both the SPP Balancing
       Authority Area where the Resource is located and to the SPP Balancing Authority Area
       where the Resource is not located. To determine the Resource’s seasonal capacity that is
       deliverable to load located within the SPP Balancing Authority Area where the Resource
       is located, the Transmission Provider will determine each Resource’s deliverable amount
       that is deliverable to load in the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area and not
       whether a particular Resource is deliverable to specific delivery points or SPP Zones. To
       determine a Resource’s seasonal capacity that is deliverable to load located within the
       SPP Balancing Authority Area where the Resource is not located, the Transmission
       Provider will determine the Deliverable Capacity amount of each Resource in the same
       SPP Balancing Authority Area by studying the deliverability of all Resources to the
       aggregate interface of the West DC Ties and determine a Deliverable Capacity amount of
       each Resource by studying the deliverability from the aggregate interface of the West DC
       Ties to the SPP Balancing Authority Area where the Resource is not located. For a
       Resource to have seasonal capacity that is deliverable to load located in a SPP Balancing
       Authority Area in which a Resource is not located, the Resource shall be limited to the
       lesser of the following: (1) the Resource’s MW amounts deliverable to the aggregate
       interface of the West DC Ties; (2) the Resource’s MW amounts from the aggregate
       interface of West DC Ties to the SPP Balancing Authority Area in which the Resource is
       not located, and (3) the firm Transmission Service capacity across the West DC Tie that
        has been reserved for the entirety of the applicable season. A Resource’s Deliverable
       Capacity amount for an applicable season is limited to the amount of Deliverable
       Capacity available to the SPP Balancing Authority Area in which the Resource is located
       plus the amount of Deliverable Capacity available to the SPP Balancing Authority Area
       in which the Resource is not located, but cannot exceed the total Net Generating Capacity
       of the Resource. The results of the Summer Season Deliverability Study shall be valid for
       the upcoming Summer Season and the subsequent Summer Season. The results of the
       Winter Season Deliverability Study shall be valid for the upcoming Winter Season and
       the subsequent Winter Season.


10.2   The Transmission Provider will utilize its current transmission planning models to
       perform the Summer Season Deliverability Study and the Winter Season Deliverability
       Study. The Transmission Provider will begin each Deliverability Study with the initial
       assumption that any Resource generating in the planning model is automatically
       deliverable to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas for which the Resource being studied
       resides for the dispatched output. A Resource’s total capacity equals the generating unit’s
       maximum output of MWs. For multiple generating units at one site, the total capacity for
       the site is the sum of maximum MWs of all generating units. A transfer level equal to the
       difference between the Resource’s maximum MW capacity and the amount dispatched in
       the planning model is determined for each Resource. Each transfer will consist of at least
       one Resource or may consist of multiple Resources grouped together, as specified in
       either the Summer Season Deliverability Study or the Winter Season Deliverability Study
       scope. A First Contingency Incremental Transfer Capability (“FCITC”) analysis of each
       transfer will be performed to determine the deliverability of the Resource. Transmission
       Facilities 100 kV and above will be included in the FCITC analysis. A three percent
       (3%) transfer distribution factor threshold will be used to analyze constraints impacted by
       the transfer.


10.3   The Summer Season Deliverability Study and the Winter Season Deliverability Study
       results for each Generator Owner’s Resource to the SPP Balancing Authority Area for
       which it is located shall consist of the total Resource’s deliverability of MW amounts to
        that SPP Balancing Authority Area. Each Generator Owner of a Jointly Owned Unit will
       coordinate to determine the MW deliverability amounts for its share of a Jointly Owned
       Unit.
       10.3.1 The Summer Season Deliverability Study and the Winter Season Deliverability
               Study results for each Generator Owner’s Resource that determines deliverability
               of capacity of the Resource to the a SPP Balancing Authority Area where the
               Resource is not located shall be limited to the lesser of the following: (1) the
               Resource’s MW amounts deliverable to the aggregate interface of the West DC
               Ties, (2) the Resource’s MW amounts from the aggregate interface of West DC
               Ties to the SPP Balancing Authority Area for which the Resource is not located,
               and (3) the firm Transmission Service capacity across the West DC Tie that has
               been reserved for the entirety of the applicable season.
       10.3.2 The availability of transmission service rights to the West DC Tie is not conveyed
               by the Deliverability Study.

10.4   The amount of Deliverable Capacity of any Resource available for purchase to meet the
       Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement shall equal the lesser of:
       a) the Resource’s Accredited Capacity less the MW amount of capacity that has been
       committed to meet for the applicable season i) Firm Capacity and ii) a sale to another
       entity; or b) the amount of a Resource’s total deliverable MWs less the MW amount of
       capacity that has been committed to meet for the applicable season i) Firm Capacity and
       ii) a sale to another entity, as determined from the Generator Owner’s Workbook.


10.5   A Generator Owner that does not submit or update a Workbook to the Transmission
       Provider by May 15th for the Summer Season or by November 15th for the Winter
       Season that contains the amount of generation capacity available through each
       Deliverability Study shall be deemed to have no Deliverable Capacity that shall not be
       entitled to receive any revenue distributions collected from Deficiency Payments.
 10.6   Demand Response Resource(s) or RRDRP(s) classified as Demand Response Program(s)
       shall not be a) eligible to be used as Deliverable Capacity and b) available for purchase to
       satisfy the Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement.


10.7   A power purchase agreement to satisfy the Pre-Season Requirement and Resource
       Adequacy Requirement based on the most recent Summer Season or Winter Season
       Deliverability Study may only rely on the results of such study for no longer than the
       upcoming Summer Season or Winter Season and the subsequent Summer Season or
       Winter Season.
       (1)    Deliverable Capacity purchases by an LRE to satisfy the Resource Adequacy
              Requirement will not require firm transmission service to support the capacity.
              Deliverable Capacity purchases shall not entitle a Market Participant to receive
              Auction Revenue Rights under Attachment AE of the Tariff.

             but are later submitted in the updated Workbook prior to November 15th
             must have an expectation of availability in accordance with Section 6.0 of
             this Attachment AA at the time the Resource is submitted in the updated
             Workbook.

      (c)    Should a Resource that is initially identified in the Workbook to be
             unavailable but subsequently becomes available or has, an expectation of
             availability in accordance with Section 6.0 of this Attachment AA at the

             Workbook by November 15th, such Resource will count as capacity for

 12.0   Post-Season AnalysisNet Peak Demand


       The Transmission Provider shall conduct a post-Summer Season and post-Winter Season
analysis to compare the LRE’s actual Net Peak Demand for each season versus the LRE’s
planning forecast. The analysis would be used to evaluate, at a minimum, LRE’s planning
forecast consistency and develop further improvements for the resource adequacy process. The
Transmission Provider will take the results to the Supply Adequacy Working Group for review
who may refer cases of potential discrepancies to the Markets and Operations Policy Committee
for further investigation and action, if necessary.

12.1   The actual Peak Demand shall be adjusted by weather normalization based on the
       individual LRE’s forecasting practices to determine the Post-Season Net Peak Demand.
       The Transmission Provider shall apply the weather normalization process, and additional
       adjustments necessary to determine the Post-Season Net Peak Demand, in accordance
       with the SPP Business Practices.

12.2   Any impact to an LRE’s actual Peak Demand from a Demand Response Resource or
       RRDRP, for which the LRE has qualified for the applicable season, shall be summed
       together and added to the applicable LRE’s actual Peak Demand hour when determining
       the actual LRE’s actual Peak Demand in accordance with the SPP Business Practices.

       (1)     In the event the actual metered load for the applicable interval is less than the
               Firm Service Level, the Demand Response Capacity of such resources shall be
               added back to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand for that same hour.

       (2)     In the event the actual metered load for the applicable interval is greater than the
               Firm Service Level, but less than the Net Generating Capacity plus the Firm
               Service Level, the amount added back to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand for that
               same hour shall be calculated as follows:

               Net Generating Capability + Firm Service Level - actual metered load

       (3)     In the event the actual metered load for the applicable interval is greater than the
               Net Generating Capacity plus the Firm Service Level, no amount shall be added
               back to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand for that same hour.
 12.3   In the event the LRE or Market Participant has not submitted in the Workbook the load
       forecasting methodology materials as outlined in the SPP Business Practices, the
       Transmission Provider shall apply a default methodology to normalize the LRE actual
       Net Peak Demand for weather related impacts the LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand
       for the applicable season.
 14.0   Resource Adequacy Assurance


14.1   Variables

       The variables used in the calculations are as follows:
       (1)    Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              The available Deliverable Capacity above the committed capacity of Generator
              Owner Resource(s) in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area as reflected in its
              completed Workbook.        Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP East
              Balancing Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season Resource
              Adequacy Requirement and the Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement.
       (2)    Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
              The available Deliverable Capacity above the committed capacity of Generator
              Owner Resource(s) in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area as reflected in its
              completed Workbook. Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP West
              Balancing Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season Resource
              Adequacy Requirement and the Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement.
       (3)    LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              The Transmission Provider will determine LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP
              East Balancing Authority Area for both the Summer Season and the Winter
              Season. The Transmission Provider will determine the LRE Deficient Capacity
              for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area as follows:
              (a)     In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is less than or
                      equal to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract
                      amount of Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of
                      this Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East
                      Balancing Authority Area shall be:
                      (i)     the Resource Adequacy Requirement of an LRE in the SPP East
                              Balancing Authority Area less the sum of Deliverable Capacity,
                              Demand Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE,;
                              or
              (ii)    zero, if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                     Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is greater than or
                     equal to the Resource Adequacy Requirement of the same LRE.
                     LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
                     Area is determined for both the Summer Season and the Winter
                     Season.
      (b)    In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is greater than
             the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
             Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
             Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
             Authority Area shall be:
             (i)     the actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
                     Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
                     Attachment AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity
                     PRM for the applicable season of the SPP East Balancing
                     Authority Area) less the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand
                     Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity; or
              (ii)   zero, if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                     Capacity, and Firm Capacity is greater than or equal to the actual
                     Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of Firm
                     Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
                     Attachment AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity
                     PRM for the applicable season of the SPP East Balancing
                     Authority Area).
(4)   LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
      The Transmission Provider will determine LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP
      West Balancing Authority Area for both the Summer Season and the Winter
      Season. The Transmission Provider will determine the LRE Deficient Capacity
      for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area as follows:
      (a)    In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is less than or
             equal to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract
       amount of Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of
      this Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West
      Balancing Authority Area shall be:
      (i)    the Resource Adequacy Requirement of an LRE in the SPP West
             Balancing Authority Area less the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand
             Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE,; or

      (ii)   zero if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
             Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is greater than or
             equal to the Resource Adequacy Requirement of the same LRE.
             LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority
             Area is determined for both the Summer Season and the Winter
             Season.
(b)   In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is greater than
      the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
      Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
      Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing
      Authority Area shall be:
       (i)   the actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
             Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
             Attachment AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity
             PRM for the applicable season of the SPP West Balancing
             Authority Area) less the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand
             Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity; or
      (ii)   zero, if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
             Capacity, and Firm Capacity is greater than or equal to the actual
             Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of Firm
             Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
             Attachment AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity
             PRM for the applicable season of the SPP West Balancing
             Authority Area).
 (5)   LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
      Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of an LRE
      in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area less Resource Adequacy Requirement
      of the same LRE, or zero if the Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
      Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is less than or equal to the
      Resource Adequacy Requirement of the same LRE. LRE Excess Capacity for the
      SPP East Balancing Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season
      and the Winter Season.
(6)   LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
      Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of an LRE
      in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area less Resource Adequacy Requirement
      of the same LRE, or zero if the Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
      Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is less than or equal to the
      Resource Adequacy Requirement of the same LRE. LRE Excess Capacity for the
      SPP West Balancing Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season
      and the Winter Season.
(7)   SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning Reserve
      Summer Season = [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand
      Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
      less the sum of all LREs’ Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the
      SPP East Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess
      Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all
      LREs’ Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP East Balancing
      Authority Area.
      Winter Season =     [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand
      Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
      less the sum of all LREs’ Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the
      SPP East Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess
      Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all
      LREs’ Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP East Balancing
      Authority Area.
 (8)    SPP West Balancing Authority Area Planning Reserve
       Summer Season = [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand
       Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       less the sum of all LREs’ Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the
       SPP West Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess
       Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all
       LREs’ Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP West
       Balancing Authority Area.
       Winter Season =     [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand
       Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       less the sum of all LREs’ Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the
       SPP West Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess
       Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all
       LREs’ Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area.
(9)    Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       A piecewise curve defined by four linear functions assessing the value of excess
       Accredited Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area based on the
       relative magnitude of Accredited Capacity to the sum of all LREs’ Resource
       Adequacy Requirement for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area.
(10)   Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       A piecewise curve defined by four linear functions assessing the value of excess
       Accredited Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area based on the
       relative magnitude of Accredited Capacity to the sum of all LREs’ Resource
       Adequacy Requirement for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.
(11)   Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       The intersection of the Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the Regional Accredited Value for the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area for the applicable Winter Season or Summer Season.
(12)   Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
        The intersection of the Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area and the Regional Accredited Value for the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area for the applicable Winter Season or Summer Season.
(13)   Regional Accredited Value for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       The total Accredited Capacity to meet the Resource Adequacy Requirement for
       the SPP East Balancing Authority Area plus the Generator Owned Excess
       Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and LRE Excess Capacity
       for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area.
(14)   Regional Accredited Value for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       The total Accredited Capacity to meet the Resource Adequacy Requirement for
       the SPP West Balancing Authority Area plus the Generator Owned Excess
       Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area and LRE Excess Capacity
       for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.
(15)   Sufficiency Charge for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area multiplied by
       the Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP East Balancing Authority
       Area.
(16)   Sufficiency Charge for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area multiplied
       by the Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area.
(17)   Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       A pro rata allocation of Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP East
       Balancing Authority Area, as described in Section 14.5 of this Attachment AA,
       used to resolve any LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
       Area.
(18)   Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       A pro rata allocation of Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP West
       Balancing Authority Area, as described in Section 14.6 of this Attachment AA,
       used to resolve any LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area.
        (19)   LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              A pro rata allocation of LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
              Authority Area, as described in Section 14.5 of this Attachment AA, used to
              resolve any LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area.
       (20)   LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
              A pro rata allocation of LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP West Balancing
              Authority Area, as described in Section 14.6 of this Attachment AA, used to
              resolve any LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.
14.2   Deficiency Payment for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area

       (1)    The Deficiency Payment shall be calculated using the applicable CONE and
              CONE Factor for both the Summer Season and Winter Season and the amount of
              LRE Deficient Capacity for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season. The
              Deficiency Payment shall only be assessed for the Resource Adequacy
              Requirement and will not be assessed for the Pre-Season Requirement. The
              Deficiency Payment assessed to the LRE shall reflect the seasonal deficiency
              quantity and the seasonal reliability need set by the CONE Factor for both seasons
              as described below:
                     Deficiency Payment = Greater of the Winter Season Deficiency Amount
                     and the Summer Season Deficiency Amount for the SPP East Balancing
                     Authority Area
              (a)    Summer Season Deficiency Amount for the SPP East Balancing Authority
                     Area = [LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
                     Area * CONE * CONE FACTOR for the Summer Season Resource
                     Adequacy Requirement for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area]

              (b)    Winter Season Deficiency Amount for the SPP East Balancing Authority
                     Area = [LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
                     Area * CONE * CONE FACTOR for the Winter Season Resource
                     Adequacy Requirement for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area]
 (c)    The CONE FACTOR for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area shall be
       determined individually for both the Summer Season and the Winter
       Season as follows:

       (i)     125% when the SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning
               Reserve is greater than or equal to the Accredited Capacity PRM
               for the applicable season plus 8%; or
       (ii)    150% when the SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning
               Reserve is greater than or equal to the Accredited Capacity PRM
               for the applicable season plus 3%, but less than the Accredited
               Capacity PRM for the applicable season plus 8%; or
       (iii)   200% when the SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning
               Reserve is less than the Accredited Capacity PRM for the
               applicable season plus 3%.
(d)    An LRE that resolves its capacity deficiency for the purpose of meeting
       the Summer Season Resource Adequacy Requirement by May 15th and
       resolves its capacity deficiency for the purpose of meeting the Winter
       Season Resource Adequacy Requirement by November 15th of the
       applicable year will be considered compliant.
(ed)   An LRE that fails to obtain sufficient capacity to meet the Summer Season
       Resource Adequacy Requirement by May 15th of the applicable year or,

14.4   Billing Procedure
               On an annual basis, the Transmission Provider shall calculate the Deficiency
       Payment amounts to be assessed against a Market Participant in the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area pursuant to Section 14.2 and
       Section 14.3 of this Attachment AA needed by the LRE to be sufficient for the applicable
       season’s Resource Adequacy Requirement. On or before December 30thSeptember 1st
       of the year after the applicable calendar year, the Transmission Provider shall submit an
       invoice to the Market Participant as a charge for the Deficiency Payment amount. The
       invoice shall be paid by the Market Participant within seven (7) calendar days of receipt.
       All payments shall be made in immediately available funds payable to the Transmission
       Provider, or by wire transfer to a bank named by the Transmission Provider. In the event
       of a dispute between the Transmission Provider and the Market Participant related to the
       calculation and assessment of a Deficiency Payment, the Market Participant shall pay the
       amount in dispute, and the Transmission Provider shall deposit into an escrow account
       the portion of the invoice in dispute, pending resolution of such dispute.


14.5   Revenue Distribution for SPP East Balancing Authority Area

              Revenues from Deficiency Payments, as allocated by the Summer Season and
       Winter Season as described in Section 14.2(4) of this Attachment AA, collected by the
       Transmission Provider for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area shall be distributed to
       Market Participant(s) for its LRE(s) with LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East
       Balancing Authority Area or Generator Owner(s) with Generator Owner Excess Capacity
       for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area on a pro rata basis according to the following
       for each season:
       (1)    In the event that the sum of all LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
              Authority Area is greater than or equal to the sum of LRE Deficient Capacity for
              the SPP East Balancing Authority Area then:

              (a)     LRE revenue =
                      (individual LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
                      Area / sum of all LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
              Authority Area) * sum of the Deficiency Payment(s) for the SPP East
             Balancing Authority Area; and
      (b)    LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area =
             (individual LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
             Area / sum of all LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
             Authority Area) * sum of the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East
             Balancing Authority Area
(2)   In the event that the sum of all LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
      Authority Area is less than the sum of LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East
      Balancing Authority Area, then the allocation of revenues shall be distributed
      according to the following steps:

      (a)    LRE revenue =

             [(individual LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority

 15.0   Accredited Capacity


15.1   Effective Load Carrying Capability Study for Wind, Solar, and Energy Storage
       Resources
       (1)   Capacity accreditation for wind resources, solar resources, and Energy Storage
             Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources, will be established
             using an Effective Load Carrying Capability (“ELCC”) Study, as described in
             Section 15.1 of this Attachment AA, SPP Business Practices and SPP Planning
             Criteria. The ELCC Study for capacity accreditation of wind resources, solar
             resources,   and   Energy   Storage   Resources,   excluding   pumped    storage
             hydroelectric resources, shall be conducted separately for the SPP East Balancing
             Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area based on which SPP
             Balancing Authority Area those Resources are located. When the term “load” is
             used in this Section 15, it is understood that the term refers to the load of the
             applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area in which the Resources being evaluated
             are located. The ELCC Study for each resource type will consist of probabilistic
             analyses utilizing the Loss of Load Expectation (“LOLE”) metric one (1) day in
             ten (10) years, or 0.1 day per year. The tier determination, simulation, and
             allocation portions for the wind or solar resources ELCC Study shall be
             performed by the Transmission Provider on an annual basis for the Summer
             Season and Winter Season. The tier determination and allocation portions for the
             Electric Storage Resources ELCC Study, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric
             resources, shall be performed by the Transmission Provider on an annual basis.
             The simulation portion for the Electric Storage Resources ELCC Study,
             excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources, shall be performed by the
             Transmission Provider for the Summer Season and Winter Season on a biennial
             basis, or more often as determined by the Transmission Provider, in accordance
             with Section 15.1(3) of this Attachment AA. The Transmission Provider, with
             input from the stakeholders, shall develop the inputs and assumptions to be
             used for ELCC study scope for each resource type. The ELCC Accredited
             Capacity as calculated in all studies and tiers shall be fully allocated to all
       resources. The results of the ELCC Study shall be valid for the upcoming Summer
      Season and Winter Season.
(2)   Set forth in this Section 15.1, wind resources, solar resources and Electric Storage
      Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources, will be assigned
      into two tiers. The Transmission Provider shall assign wind resources, solar
      resources, and Electric Storage Resources, excluding pumped storage
      hydroelectric resources into tiers for each resource type as follows:
      (a)    Tier 1 – Designated Resources, resources associated with Firm Point-to-
             Point Transmission Service, and other resources with firm transmission
             service (with transmission service from those resources being accepted by
             the Transmission Provider by June 1 for the Summer Season and
             December 1 for the Winter Season) for the designated amount.

      (b)    Tier 2 – Remaining resources that do not meet the requirements of Tier 1
             for the applicable season.

(3)   ELCC studies for each resource type studied pursuant to Section 15.1 of this
      Attachment AA will consist of a base case and one or more change cases utilizing,
      at least, the prior forty (40) historical weather years. The base case is defined as
      system load supplied by all other resource types in the SPP East Balancing
      Authority Area or the SPP West Balancing Authority Area that are not being
      evaluated.

      (a)    Wind and Solar Resources
             (i)     The wind ELCC Study base case will include load, conventional
                     resources, solar resources, hydroelectric resources, Energy Storage
                     Resources, and all other resources except for wind resources. The
                     solar ELCC Study base case will include load, conventional
                     resources, wind resources, hydroelectric resources, Energy Storage
                     Resources, and all other resources except for solar resources. The
                     first change case for the wind resources and solar resources will
                     include Tier 1 wind resources or Tier 1 solar resources, as
                     applicable. The second change case will include all wind or all
              solar resources. The base case and all change cases for the wind
             resources and solar resources will be analyzed by adding or
             removing the same amount of load in every hour of the assessment
             period until a total LOLE of 0.1 day per year is achieved across the
             totality of the historical weather years analyzed for the applicable
             season. The amount of load added or removed in each change case
             will be compared to the amount of load added in the base case to
             derive an ELCC megawatt (“MW”) for each change case across the
             totality of the historical weather years analyzed. The difference in
             total ELCC MW of the base case and the first change case is the
             ELCC MW assigned to Tier 1. The difference in total ELCC MW
             of the first change case and the second change case is the ELCC
             MW assigned to Tier 2.
(b)   Electric Storage Resources
      (i)    The Electric Storage Resource ELCC Study base case will include
             load, conventional resources, wind resources, solar resources,
             hydroelectric resources, and all other resources except for Electric
             Storage Resources that are not pumped storage hydroelectric
             resources. In the Electric Storage Resources ELCC Study, the
             storage resources will be scheduled to dispatch during high net
             load hours, which may cause the resource to be unavailable to meet
             a reliability need outside of the peak hours.

      (ii)   The simulation portion of the Electric Storage Resources ELCC
             Study shall analyze equipment with the durations listed below,
             defined by the equipment parameters. An ELCC curve based on
             penetration and accreditation percentage shall be established for
             each defined duration type. Each penetration amount will be
             analyzed by adding or removing the same amount of load in every
             hour of the assessment period until a total LOLE of 0.1 day per
             year is achieved across the totality of the historical weather years
             analyzed for the applicable season. The most recent ELCC curve
                             for each duration type shall be used for the allocation portion of the
                            Electric Storage Resource ELCC Study, as specified in Section
                            15.2 (2)(c)-(h) of this Attachment AA.

                            (a)    Eight hour duration equipment

                            (b)    Six hour duration equipment

                            (c)    Four hour duration equipment

15.2   Allocation to Individual ELCC Resources

       (1)   Wind and Solar Resources
             Once the total Accredited Capacity has been determined for each tier of wind and
             solar resource, each individual wind or solar resource will be assigned a
             percentage of the total Accredited Capacity of its corresponding tier. Tier 1 wind
             resources or solar resources will receive allocation, for each applicable season,
             based on the average production output of the individual resource during the top
             three percent (3%) Net Peak Load hours of the LRE in accordance with the SPP
             Planning Criteria. Full or partial forced events identified as Outside Management
             Control (“OMC”), as defined by NERC, that impact the production output of an
             individual resource included in Tier 1 shall be excluded from the determination of
             allocation of wind resources and solar resources in Tier 1. Individual resources of
             Tier 1 will then receive a pro-rata share of the total Accredited Capacity
             compared to the total historical average capacity value of all other wind resources
             or solar resources in the tier. Tier 2 wind resources and solar resources will
             receive allocation, for each applicable season, based on the average historical
             production output from the top three percent (3%) Net Peak Load hours of the
             applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area’s load in accordance with the SPP
             Planning Criteria. Full or partial forced events identified as OMC, as defined by
             NERC, that impact the production output of an individual resource included in
             Tier 2 shall be excluded from the determination of allocation of wind resources
             and solar resources in Tier 2. Individual resources of Tier 2 will then receive a
       pro-rata share of the total Accredited Capacity compared to the total historical
      average capacity value of all other wind resources and solar resources in Tier 2.

(2)   Electric Storage Resources
      (a)    The total penetration of Electric Storage Resources will dictate the
             percentage of accreditation that all Electric Storage Resources will receive
             based on each Tier and duration, regardless of location of the resource.
             The Transmission Provider shall perform the allocation process of the
             ELCC Study for Electric Storage Resources annually and shall utilize the
             most recent ELCC curves for each duration type in the process.

      (b)    Electric Storage Resources in Tier 1 will be prioritized before resources in
             Tier 2 when determining the Electric Storage Resource’s Accredited
             Capacity. All duration types will be prioritized in the order specified in
             Section 15.2(2)(c)-(h) of this Attachment AA within each tier. Resources
             that do not meet an hourly duration curve will be rounded down to the
             nearest hourly duration established. For an Electric Storage Resource to be
             allocated capacity with a higher duration within the same tier, the LRE
             shall notify the Transmission Provider and that resource must be de-rated
             to appropriate duration timeframe studied. Two hour Electric Storage
             Resources will have its Accredited Capacity determined with four hour
             duration Energy Storage Resources and shall receive no more than 50%
             accreditation.

      (c)    Eight hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 1 will be
             assigned the ELCC percentage of the eight hour duration curve for the
             total penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources identified as eight
             hour duration and Tier 1 for the applicable season;

      (d)    Six hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 1 will be
             assigned the ELCC percentage of the six hour duration curve for the total
             penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
             identified as:
       (i)     Tier 1 Eight hour duration; and

      (ii)    Tier 1 Six hour duration.

(e)   Four hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 1 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the four hour duration curve for the total
      penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
      identified as:

      (i)     Tier 1 Eight hour duration;

      (ii)    Tier 1 Six hour duration; and

      (iii)   Tier 1 Four hour duration

(f)   Eight hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 2 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the eight hour duration curve for the
      total penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable
      season identified as:

      (i)     All duration types of tier 1; and

      (ii)    Tier 2 Eight hour duration.

(g)   Six hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 2 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the six hour duration curve for the total
      penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
      identified as:

      (i)     All duration types of tier 1;

      (ii)    Tier 2 Eight hour duration; and

      (iii)   Tier 2 Six hour duration

(h)   Four hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 2 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the six hour duration curve for the total
      penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
      identified as:
                      (i)     All duration types of tier 1;

                     (ii)     Tier 2 Eight hour duration;

                     (iii)   Tier 2 Six hour duration; and

                     (iv)    Tier 2 Four hour duration.

15.3   System ELCC Study

              An annual system ELCC Study shall be conducted by the Transmission Provider
       for the Summer Season and Winter Season separately for both the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area to ensure the capacity value
       in the individual ELCC Studies is equivalent to the capacity value of the total system
       ELCC Study for the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area. The system ELCC Study
       base case will include load and all resources except for wind resources, solar resources,
       and Energy Storage Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources. The
       system change case will include all resources and load. The difference in the total ELCC
       MW of the system base case and the ELCC MW of the system change case is the system
       ELCC MW. The capacity value determined in the system ELCC study shall be applied to
       the individual ELCC Studies for wind, solar, and Energy Storage Resource ELCC Studies
       on a pro rata basis according to the individual ELCC Studies.


15.4   Accredited Capacity Determination for Conventional Resources
       (1)    Each conventional resource’s Accredited Capacity shall be determined using a)
              the Net Generating Capability and b) the resource’s Conventional Resource
              Performance Adjustment for the applicable season. The resource’s Conventional
              Resource Performance Adjustment shall be determined using the resource’s a)
              EFORd for the applicable season and b) EFOF adjusted for Incremental Outage
              Impact of the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area for the applicable season.
              The individual resource’s adjusted EFOF is dependent upon the Incremental
              Outage Impact compared to the EFOF impact of all conventional resources of the
              applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area.            The Conventional Resource
              Performance Adjustment shall not exceed 100% for an individual resource. The
       Accredited Capacity and Conventional Resource Performance Adjustment
      calculations are as follows:

      Accredited Capacity
            =Net Generating Capability × (1 – Conventional Resource Performance
      Adjustment)
      Where:
      Conventional Resource Performance Adjustment
      = EFORd + (EFOF x Incremental Outage Impact / total system EFOF impact)
      Total system EFOF impact = Sum of [Net Generating Capability x EFOF] from
      all conventional resources of the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area
(2)   The Transmission Provider shall determine a resource’s Conventional Resource
      Performance Adjustment in accordance with Section 15.4 of this Attachment AA
      and the SPP Business Practices. The full and partial forced outage events that
      occurred shall be used when determining the resource’s Conventional Resource
      Performance Adjustment. Authorized Outages (either full or partial) shall not be
      considered when calculating the resource’s Conventional Resource Performance
      Adjustment. The resulting EFORd and adjusted EFOF for an individual resource
      will be added together when determining the Conventional Resource Performance
      Adjustment for the applicable season.

      (a)      EFORd

               (i)    The EFORd shall be determined on an individual historical year
                      basis and averaged together considering all appropriate historical
                      years for the applicable season. A resource’s EFORd shall include
                      events occurring during the entire applicable season and exclude
                      OMC events, as defined by NERC.

               (ii)   The Transmission Provider shall calculate and post a weighted
                      class average EFORd for each applicable season. The weighted
                      class average EFORd shall be determined separately for the SPP
                      East Balancing Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing
                      Authority Area. The resources shall be weighted against all other
              resources in the same class and in the same applicable SPP
             Balancing Authority Area for determining class average EFORd.
             The weighted class average EFORd shall be determined as
             follows:

             Sum of [Net Generating Capability x EFORd] from resources
             within the class / Sum of Net Generating Capability from resources
             within the class

(b)   EFOF

      (i)    The EFOF shall be determined on an individual historical year
             basis and averaged together considering all appropriate historical
             years for the applicable season. A resource’s EFOF shall include
             events occurring during the top three percent (3%) Adjusted Net
             Peak Load hours for the applicable season for each historical year.
             Certain OMC events, as defined in the SPP Business Practices,
             shall be included when determining the resource’s EFOF.

      (ii)   The Transmission Provider shall calculate and post a weighted
             class average EFOF for each applicable season. The weighted class
             average EFOF shall be determined separately for the SPP East
             Balancing Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority
             Area. The resources shall be weighted against all other resources
             in the same class and in the same applicable SPP Balancing
             Authority Area for determining class average EFOF. The class
             average EFOF shall be calculated prior to the application of
             Incremental Outage Impact. The weighted class average EFOF
             shall be determined as follows:

             Sum of [Net Generating Capability x EFOF] from resources within
             the class / Sum of Net Generating Capability from resources within
             the class
                     (iii)   The resource’s EFOF shall be further adjusted for Incremental
                            Outage Impact. The Incremental Outage Impact shall be
                            determined by the Transmission Provider on a biennial basis in
                            accordance with the LOLE Study scope. The impact on the Base
                            PRM between a scenario including the modeled incremental
                            correlated forced outages and another scenario without the
                            incremental correlated forced outages shall be calculated and set as
                            the Incremental Outage Impact. The same amount of load shall be
                            added or removed in every hour of the assessment period until a
                            resulting LOLE is achieved across the totality of the historical
                            weather years analyzed for the applicable season and the resulting
                            LOLE is equivalent between the two scenarios. The Incremental
                            Outage Impact shall be determined separately for the SPP East
                            Balancing Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority
                            Area.

                    (iv)    In the event the Transmission Provider does not determine a
                            resource’s EFOF prior to the first season the resource is qualified
                            under this Attachment AA, the resource’s EFOF determined by the
                            entity shall not be adjusted for Incremental Outage Impact for the
                            first applicable season.

       (3)   Resources internal to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas qualified under this
             Attachment AA where historical performance data exists but is not provided for
             the applicable season shall have 100% EFORd and 100% EFOF applied to the
             applicable historical year and season in determining the resource’s Conventional
             Resource Performance Adjustment. Once a resource has been qualified, the
             Generator Owner, LRE, or Market Participant providing the historical data shall
             continually submit historical performance data to avoid a 100% EFORd and
             100% EFOF applied to the applicable historical year and season.

             season as follows:
             (i)     availability and performance during the top three percent (3%)
                     Adjusted Net Peak Load hours of the applicable SPP Balancing
                     Authority Area;
             (ii)    availability and performance during all intervals when the
                     applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area is in conservative
                     operations advisory or any level of EEA Emergency Condition;
                     and
             (iii)   performance during intervals when instructed to deploy by the
                     Transmission Provider.


      (b)    A Conservative Operations Demand Response Program’s Demand
             Response Performance Adjustment shall consider performance and
             availability for the applicable season as follows:
              (i)     availability and performance during all intervals when the
                     applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area is in conservative
                     operations advisory or any level of EEA Emergency Condition;
                     and
             (ii)    performance during intervals when instructed to deploy by the
                     Transmission Provider.
      (c)    An Emergency Demand Response Program’s Demand Response
             Performance Adjustment shall consider the performance for the applicable
             season as follows:
             (i)     availability and performance during all intervals when the
                     applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area is in any level of EEA
                     Emergency Condition; and
             (ii)    performance during intervals when instructed to deploy by the
                     Transmission Provider.


(4)   The Transmission Provider shall determine a reliability-based Accredited
      Capacity limit for Emergency Demand Response Programs (“Emergency DR
      Limit”) and apply such limit in accordance with this Attachment AA and SPP
      Business Practices. The Emergency DR Limit shall be set in the SPP Planning
      Criteria and reviewed by the Transmission Provider on an as needed basis. Any
      change to the Emergency DR Limit shall be made no later than one year prior to
      the first applicable season.

(5)   An LRE’s total amount of qualified Demand Response Capacity for Emergency
      Demand Response Programs shall not exceed such LRE’s portion of the
      Emergency DR Limit for the applicable season.

 1.1    Definitions C

CFTC
The Commodity Futures Trading Commission


Combined Interest Resource
A Resource registered to reflect shared interest among multiple Asset Owners who elect to
model as one commercial Resource. Credits and charges for these Resources are allocated post
market using the submitted interest share percentages.


Commercial Model
A representation of the attributes of and the relationships between Balancing Authority Areas,
Market Participants, Asset Owners, Resource and load assets and Price Nodes for use in the
Integrated Marketplace.


Commercial Operation
As defined in Attachment V of this Tariff.


Commitment Instruction
An instruction issued by the Transmission Provider or a local transmission operator to a Market
Participant in the Day-Ahead Market, any Reliability Unit Commitment process, or the Multi-
Day Reliability Assessment to (i) either start up or shut down a specified Resource and/or (ii)
transition an MCR from one configuration to another.


Commit Time
The time specified by the Transmission Provider or a local transmission operator in a
Commitment Instruction at which a Resource is to be synchronized and operating at or above its
Minimum Economic Capacity Operating Limit. For an MSR, this is the time specified by the
Transmission Provider or a local transmission operator in a Commitment Instruction at which the
Resource should be connected and at or above its Minimum Discharge Limit or its Minimum
Charge Limit.
 Common Bus
A single bus to which two or more Resources owned by the same Asset Owner are connected in
an electrically equivalent manner where such Resources may be treated as interchangeable for
certain compliance monitoring purposes.


Confidential Information
As referenced within Attachments AE, AF and AG to this Tariff, information containing or
revealing:
(1)    (a)    Any confidential, proprietary, or commercially sensitive information, or
              information of a plan, specification, pattern, procedure, design, device, list,
              concept, policy or compilation relating to the present or planned business of a
              Market Participant that is conspicuously designated as Confidential Information
              in writing, on each page of the document, by disclosing party at the time the
              information is provided to receiving party, whether conveyed electronically, in
              writing, through inspection, or otherwise;
       (b)    Any confidential, proprietary, or commercially sensitive information, or
              information of a plan, specification, pattern, procedure, design, device, list,
              concept, policy or compilation relating to the present or planned business of a
              Market Participant that is provided orally and designated as Confidential
              Information by disclosing party at the time the information is provided to
              receiving party;
       (c)    Any customer information designated by the customer as proprietary, unless the
              customer has authorized the release for public disclosure of such information;
       (d)    Any software, products of software or other vendor information that the
              Transmission Provider is required to keep confidential under its agreements.
(2)    Confidential Information does not include Critical Energy Infrastructure Information
       (“CEII”) materials as designated by FERC, which must be obtained in accordance with
       FERC regulations.
 Conservative Operations Demand Response Program
As defined in Attachment AA of the Tariff.


Contingency
As defined in the NERC Glossary of Terms Used in NERC Reliability Standards.


Contingency Reserve
Qualified Resource capacity held in reserve for Contingencies that is the sum of Spinning
Reserve and Supplemental Reserve. Calculated for each SPP Balancing Authority Area.


Contingency Reserve Deployment Instruction
An instruction to address a Contingency event issued by the Transmission Provider to Resources
in the corresponding SPP Balancing Authority Area that cleared Contingency Reserve in the
Real-Time Balancing Market to deploy a specific Megawatt quantity of Contingency Reserve as
communicated as a component of the Setpoint Instructions.


Contingency Reserve Deployment Period
The time allowed to deploy Contingency Reserve following the issuance of a Contingency
Reserve Deployment Instruction, as specified in the Market Protocols.


Contingency Reserve Scarcity Factor
A multiplier used to define a shortage of Contingency Reserve in a Reserve Zone and the
appropriate scarcity price value associated with the shortage.


Control Status
A parameter communicated electronically to the Transmission Provider by a Market Participant
at any time during an Operating Hour indicating a Resource’s ability to follow Setpoint
Instructions.


Coordinated Flowgate
 A flowgate defined within a joint operating agreement between the Transmission Provider and
another transmission provider as being affected by the transmission of Energy on either party’s
transmission system.


Critical Load
Load that is: (1) critical to delivering natural gas, fuel oil, or other necessary fuels to generators;
or (2) identified as critical by an applicable regulatory authority.


Current Operating Plan
The Transmission Provider’s internal hourly Resource commitment schedule for the Operating
Day resulting from the Day-Ahead Market and Day-Ahead Reliability Unit Commitment
processes and updated, as required, during the Intra-Day Reliability Unit Commitment process
that is used as input into the Real-Time Balancing Market.
 1.1    Definitions E

Electrical Node (“ENode”)
A physical node represented in the Network Model where electrical equipment and components
are connected.


Electric Storage Resource (“ESR”)
As defined in Section 1 of the Tariff.


Electric Storage Resource Loss Factor
The factor that represents round-trip efficiency related to the amount of Energy an ESR loses
from charge to discharge. This loss factor is the ratio of (1) the Energy the ESR is able to inject
via discharge to (2) the Energy withdrawn in order to store that charge.


Eligible Entity
A Transmission Customer or Market Participant having firm SPP Transmission Service or firm
non-SPP transmission service (referred to as a “grandfathered agreement” or “GFA”) into, out
of, within or through the SPP Region.


Emergency Condition
As defined in Section 1 of the Tariff.


Emergency Demand Response Program
As defined in Attachment AA of the Tariff.


Energy
An amount of electricity that is Bid or Offered, produced, purchased, consumed, sold or
transmitted over a period of time, which is measured or calculated in Megawatt hours.


Energy and Operating Reserve Markets
As defined in Section 1 of the Tariff.
 Energy Offer Curve
A set of price/quantity pairs that consists of Megawatts and dollars per Megawatt hour with up to
ten (10) price/quantity pairs.


Excess Regulation-Down Mileage
The amount calculated under Section 8.6.2 of this Attachment AE.


Excess Regulation-Up Mileage
The amount calculated under Section 8.6.2 of this Attachment AE.


Expected Regulation-Down Mileage
The amount of Regulation-Down Service MW cleared multiplied by the Regulation-Down
Mileage Factor.


Expected Regulation-Up Mileage
The amount of Regulation-Up Service MW cleared multiplied by the Regulation-Up Mileage
Factor.


Export Interchange Transaction
A Market Participant schedule for exporting Energy out of an SPP Balancing Authority Area into
an external Balancing Authority Area.


Export Interchange Transaction Bid
A proposal by a Market Participant to purchase a fixed or price sensitive amount of Energy for
delivery outside of an SPP Balancing Authority Area at a specified External Interface and for a
period of time.


External Dynamic Resource
A registered Resource that represents one or more resources, located external to an SPP
Balancing Authority Area, which is dynamically scheduled into or out of the SPP Balancing
Authority Area.
 External Interface
A Settlement Location representing a physical interconnection point(s) between one of the SPP
Balancing Authority Areas and an external Balancing Authority Area.
 1.1        Definitions L

Load Serving Entity (“LSE”)
A distribution utility or an electric utility that has a service obligation, where a service
obligation, as defined in Section 217(a) of the Federal Power Act, means a requirement
applicable to, or the exercise of authority granted to, an electric utility under Federal, State, or
local law or under long-term contracts to provide electric service to end-users or to a distribution
utility.


Local Emergency Condition
A condition or situation determined by the local transmission operator that is imminently likely
to cause a material adverse effect on the security of or damage to the local transmission
operator’s facilities not modeled by the Transmission Provider.


Local Reliability Issue
A local voltage or reliability condition necessitating a Local Reliability Issue Commitment or, a
Curtailment of a CHILL, or a Reliability Registered Demand Response Program deployment.


Local Reliability Issue Commitment
A Resource commitment in addition to, or in lieu of, commitments resulting from the Security
Constrained Unit Commitment in the Day-Ahead Market or any Reliability Unit Commitment, in
order to mitigate Local Reliability Issues, including providing assistance to an adjacent
Balancing Authority Area, to address local reliability concerns. These Resource commitment
requirements are established prior to or during an Operating Day and are based on projected
local reliability requirements, operational considerations, and Resource and transmission
Outages. These commitments will be based on Operating Guides for recurring local voltage and
reliability requirements, but an Operating Guide is not required prior to a Resource commitment
being designated as a Local Reliability Issue Commitment. Resource commitments to relieve a
potential or actual Interconnection Reliability Operating Limit violation will not be designated in
this category.


Local Settlement Area
 A Settlement Area defined for purposes of the local allocation of costs pursuant to Section 8.6.44
of this Attachment AE.


Locational Marginal Price (“LMP”)
The price for Energy at a given Price Node which is equivalent to the marginal cost of serving
demand at the Price Node while meeting the Transmission Provider Operating Reserve
requirements in the respective Balancing Authority Area where the Price Node is located.


Long-Term Congestion Right (“LTCR”)
An instrument that entitles the holder to a Transmission Congestion Right over a period of more
than one year, which is awarded during the Transmission Provider’s annual Long-Term
Congestion Rights allocation process.


Loss Pool
A collection (a) of all Settlement Locations within a Settlement Area (“Settlement Area Loss
Pool”), or (b) defined by Trading Hub, Resource Hub, and External Interface Settlement
Locations contained within an SPP Balancing Authority Area (“SPP Balancing Authority Area
Loss Pool”).
 1.1    Definitions R

Ramp Capability Down

An Operating Reserve product, procured by the Transmission Provider from a Resource capable
of following Setpoint Instructions, that is reserved to provide downward flexibility during
periods in which net obligations decrease in future Dispatch Intervals. There is no explicit offer
for this product. The value is derived using loss of opportunity.



Ramp Capability Up

An Operating Reserve product, procured by the Transmission Provider from a Resource capable
of following Setpoint Instructions, that is reserved to provide upward flexibility during periods in
which net obligations increase in future Dispatch Intervals. There is no explicit offer for this
product. The value is derived using loss of opportunity.



Ramp-Rate-Down

A curve specifying MW/minute ramp rates applicable between Resource operating ranges that is
used to dispatch Resources in the down direction. For MSRs, Ramp-Rate-Down is the rate at
which a MSR can move from zero output to Maximum Charge Limit, which is represented as a
negative (-) value for the MW breakpoint. This rate also represents the rate at which the MSR
can move from Maximum Discharge Limit to zero output.


Ramp-Rate-Up
A curve specifying MW/minute ramp rates applicable between Resource operating ranges that is
used to dispatch Resources in the up direction. For MSRs, Ramp-Rate-Up is the rate at which a
MSR can move from zero output to Maximum Discharge Limit. This rate also represents the
rate at which the MSR can move from Maximum Charge Limit, which is represented as a
negative (-) value for the MW breakpoint, to zero output.
 Real-Time
The continuous time period during which the Real-Time Balancing Market is operated.


Real-Time Balancing Market (“RTBM”)
As defined in Section 1 of the Tariff.


Real-Time Capability
The amount (MW) of real power output the Resource is capable of instantaneously producing,
excluding any dispatch, deployment, or curtailment instructions.


Real-Time Load Ratio Share
The sum of a Market Participant’s Billable Metered Load, Self-Charging MSRs, and Export
Interchange Transactions at all Settlement Locations within an SPP Balancing Authority Area
divided by the sum of all Market Participants’ Billable Metered Load, Self-Charging MSRs, and
Export Interchange Transactions at all Settlement Locations within that respective SPP
Balancing Authority Area for a given hour.


Reciprocal Coordinated Flowgate
A Coordinated Flowgate defined within a joint operating agreement between SPP and another
transmission provider as being affected by the transmission of Energy on both of their respective
transmission systems.


Reference Bus
The location on the Transmission System in the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area
relative to which all mathematical quantities, including shift factors and penalty factors relating
to physical operation, will be calculated.


Regulation Deployment
The utilization of Regulation-Up Service and/or Regulation-Down Service through automatic
generation control equipment to automatically and continuously adjust Resource output to
balance the real power requirements of an SPP Balancing Authority Area.
 Regulation-Down
An Operating Reserve product procured by the Transmission Provider from qualified Resources
that reduce their energy output (or increase consumption of the Demand Response Load
associated with a qualified Dispatchable Demand Response Resource) in response to a
Regulation Deployment instruction from the Transmission Provider. Calculated for each SPP
Balancing Authority Area.


Regulation-Down Mileage Factor
A factor determined through historical Regulation Deployment analysis that represents the ratio
of the total Actual Regulation-Down Mileage from all Resources to the Transmission Provider’s
total cleared Regulation-Down Service for each SPP Balancing Authority Area.


Regulation-Down Mileage Offer
The price at which a Regulation Qualified Resource or a Regulation-Down Qualified Resource
has agreed to sell Expected Regulation-Down Mileage.


Regulation-Down Offer
The price at which a Regulation Qualified Resource or a Regulation-Down Qualified Resource
has committed to sell Regulation-Down.


Regulation-Down Qualified Resource
A Resource that has met the requirements to be eligible to submit Regulation-Down Offers and
Regulation-Down Mileage Offers into the Energy and Operating Reserve Markets.


Regulation-Down Scarcity Factor
A multiplier used to determine appropriate scarcity price value associated with the shortage of
Regulation-Down.
 Regulation-Down Service
The provision of Actual Regulation-Down Mileage associated with cleared Regulation-Down
Service MW in response to Regulation Deployment instructions.


Regulation-Down Service Offer
The sum of (i) a Resource’s Regulation-Down Mileage Offer multiplied by the Regulation-Down
Mileage Factor and (ii) that Resource’s Regulation-Down Offer.


Regulation Mileage Operating Tolerance
The allowable percentage deviation below a Resource’s Instructed Regulation-Up Mileage
and/or Instructed Regulation-Down Mileage over the Dispatch Interval where the Resource will
settle based upon Instructed Regulation-Up Mileage and/or Instructed Regulation-Down Mileage
versus Actual Regulation-Up and/or Actual Regulation-Down Mileage. Such percentage is set at
5%. Calculated for each SPP Balancing Authority Area.


Regulation Qualified Resource
A Resource that has met the requirements to be eligible to submit Regulation-Up Offers,
Regulation-Up Mileage Offers, Regulation-Down Offers and Regulation-Down Mileage Offers
into the Energy and Operating Reserve Markets.


Regulation Ramp Rate

A curve specifying MW/minute ramp rates that are used to determine a Resource’s maximum
Regulation-Up Service and/or Regulation-Down Service quantities.



Regulation Response Time
The maximum amount of time allowed for a Resource to move its output from zero (0)
Regulation Deployment to the full amount of Regulation-Up cleared or to move from zero (0)
Regulation Deployment to the full amount of Regulation-Down cleared.


Regulation-Up
 An Operating Reserve product procured by the Transmission Provider from qualified Resources
that increase their energy output (or reduce consumption of the Demand Response Load
associated with a qualified Dispatchable Demand Response Resource) in response to a
Regulation Deployment instruction from the Transmission Provider. Calculated for each SPP
Balancing Authority Area.


Regulation-Up Mileage Factor
A factor determined through historical Regulation Deployment analysis that represents the ratio
of the total Actual Regulation-Up Mileage from all Resources to the Transmission Provider’s
total cleared Regulation-Up Service for each SPP Balancing Authority Area.


Regulation-Up Mileage Offer
The price at which a Regulation Qualified Resource or a Regulation-Up Qualified Resource has
agreed to sell Expected Regulation-Up Mileage.


Regulation-Up Offer
The price at which a Regulation Qualified Resource or a Regulation-Up Qualified Resource has
committed to sell Regulation-Up.


Regulation-Up Qualified Resource
A Resource that has met the requirements to be eligible to submit Regulation-Up Offers and
Regulation-Up Mileage Offers into the Energy and Operating Reserve Markets.


Regulation-Up Scarcity Factor
A multiplier used to determine appropriate scarcity price value associated with the shortage of
Regulation-Up.


Regulation-Up Service
The provision of Actual Regulation-Up Mileage associated with cleared Regulation-Up Service
MW in response to Regulation Deployment instructions.
 Regulation-Up Service Offer
The sum of (i) a Resource’s Regulation-Up Mileage Offer multiplied by the Regulation-Up
Mileage Factor and (ii) that Resource’s Regulation-Up Offer.


Reliability Registered Demand Response Program (“RRDRP”)
As defined in Attachment AA of the Tariff.


Reliability Unit Commitment (“RUC”)
The process performed by the Transmission Provider to assess resource and Operating Reserve
adequacy for the Operating Day, commit or de-commit resource as necessary, and communicate
commitment or de-commitment of Resources to the appropriate Market Participants as
necessary.


Reliability Unit Commitment Period (“RUC Commitment Period”)
The contiguous period of time between a Resource’s Reliability Unit Commitment Commit Time
and Reliability Unit Commitment De-Commit Time.


Reported Load
The MWh quantity withdrawn from the transmission grid at a Meter Data Submittal Location, as
submitted by the Meter Agent. For Meter Data Submittal Locations not submitted by the Meter
Agent, State Estimator values for those locations are used.


Reservation Capacity
The reservation Megawatt between a specified source and sink associated with SPP
Transmission Service.


Reserve Sharing Event
A request for assistance to deploy Contingency Reserve by any member of a Reserve Sharing
Group following a qualifying event specified in a Reserve Sharing Group agreement.


Reserve Sharing Group
 As defined in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff.


Reserve Zone
A zone within or consisting of an SPP Balancing Authority Area containing a specific group of
Price Nodes for which a minimum and maximum Operating Reserve requirement is calculated.


Resettlement
The settlement of an Operating Day subsequent to the posting of the S120 Scheduled Settlement
Statement for that Operating Day.


Residual Load
The sum of (1) injections at each Meter Data Submittal Location within the Settlement Area and
(2) withdrawals at each Meter Data Submittal Location within the Settlement Area and (3) the
sum of all Energy into and out of a Settlement Area.
Resource
As defined in Part I, Section 1 of this Tariff.


Resource Hub
A Settlement Location consisting of an aggregation of Resource Price Nodes developed for
financial and trading purposes.


Resource Offer
For a Resource, the combination of its Start-Up Offer, No-Load Offer, Energy Offer Curve,
Transition State Offer, Regulation-Up Service Offer, Regulation-Down Service Offer, Spinning
Reserve Offer, Supplemental Reserve Offer, Uncertainty Reserve Offer, and Resource physical
operating parameters.

RTBM As-Dispatched Fixed Withdrawal

The minimum withdrawal limit that results from the MSR's applicable Maximum Discharge
Limit or Minimum Charge Limit and the MSR's Regulation-Up, Spinning Reserve, and
 Supplemental Reserve offers with Dispatch Status of “Fixed” in effect when the MSR was
originally dispatched.


RTBM Effective Control Mode

An RTBM output indicating a Resource’s status after factoring in the Resource’s Control Status,
Offer parameters, Real-Time topology, and regulation selection from the Current Operating Plan.
This parameter shares the same range of potential values as Control Status.


RUC As-Committed Fixed Withdrawal

The minimum withdrawal limit that results from the MSR's applicable Maximum Discharge
Limit or Minimum Charge Limit and the MSR's Regulation-Up, Spinning Reserve, and
Supplemental Reserve offers with Dispatch Status of “Fixed” in effect when the MSR was
originally committed by the Reliability Unit Commitment process.
