             The Transmission Provider will notify the applicable retail provider and the
      relevant electric retail regulatory authority of the pending registration, and the expected
      maximum MW level of participation, and the retail account numbers of the participating
      end-use retail customers. Additional notification will be provided if modifications are
      made to the expected megawatt level of participation. If either the relevant electric retail
      regulatory authority or retail provider disputes the accuracy of the pending registration
      information or attestations, the Transmission Provider will notify the Market Participant
      of the dispute and may pause the Resource’s registration, prohibit the Resource in
      question from participating in the Energy and Operating Reserve Markets, or not accept
      the modification until the issue is resolved between the Market Participant and the
      disputing entity. If resolution has not been reached between the registering Market

      provider, within 90 days of the Market Participant’s notification of the dispute, the
      Resource’s pending registration or the modification to the existing registration may be
      cancelled.
 2.25   Load Participating in Reliability Registered Demand Response Programs


(1)    All loads participating in Reliability Registered Demand Response Programs
       (“RRDRPs”) pursuant to Attachment AA must have the RRDRP registered by a Market
       Participant. Market Participants registering RRDRPs must identify the point of
       interconnection of the controllable load of the RRDRP. Market Participants may add,
       modify, or remove RRDRPs in accordance with the timelines specified in the Market
       Protocols. An RRDRP must be capable of producing and maintaining a response of at
       least 0.1 Megawatts for a continuous duration of sixty (60) minutes to be eligible to
       register. An RRDRP is not considered a “Resource” as that term is defined in the
       Common Service Provisions of this Tariff.
(2)    An RRDRP must have a corresponding Demand Response Load. The Demand Response
       Load may be associated with an aggregated Price Node that contains multiple electrically
       equivalent Price Nodes, provided that such aggregated Price Node is served by the same
       retail provider.
(3)    A Market Participant registering an RRDRP must submit a letter of attestation pursuant
       to Section 14.0 of this Attachment AE, and must update such letter of attestation as
       necessary.
 3.3.1   Day-Ahead Market and RTBM SCED

        The SCED used in the Day-Ahead Market and RTBM produces both a dispatch solution
and a pricing solution. The dispatch solution and pricing solution are executed independent of
each other. The MW quantities used in settlements for the dispatch and clearing of Energy and
Operating Reserves result from the dispatch solution. Except where specified as DLMP, prices
used in settlements result from the pricing solution and will be specified as LMP, MCC, MCP,
MEC, and MLC. The DLMP results from the dispatch solution. The differences between the
dispatch solution and the pricing solution are:
 (1)    SCED dispatch solution

         (a)   Co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves is based on the Energy Offers
               and Bids and Operating Reserve Offers submitted by the Market Participants.

  (2)   SCED pricing solution

         (a)   For non-FSRs, co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves is based on the
               Energy Offers and Bids and Operating Reserve Offers submitted by the Market
               Participants.
         (b)   For FSRs committed by the Transmission Provider, including FSRs committed at
               the request of a local transmission operator, but not including self-committed
               FSRs, the Transmission Provider calculates a composite Energy Offer for use in
               the co-optimization of Energy and Operating Reserves. The composite Energy
               Offer will be calculated and applied as follows:

                 (i)   The Transmission Provider calculates a composite Energy Offer for an
                       FSR by modifying each price point on the Energy Offer Curve for each
                       market interval of the Minimum Run Time by adding amortized start-up
                       and no-load costs. For FSRs that are MSRs, the composite Energy Offer
                       applies only to the discharge portion of the Energy Offer curve.

                         1. The commitment costs (i.e. start-up cost and no-load cost) in effect
                               at the time of the commitment are amortized over the Maximum
                               Economic Capacity Operating Limit and the Minimum Run Time.
                         a. The start-up cost added to each breakpoint of the Energy
                             Offer Curve is calculated by dividing the Start-Up Offer by
                             the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit and by
                             the Minimum Run Time rounded up to the nearest interval.
                        b. The no-load cost added to each breakpoint of the Energy
                             Offer Curve is calculated by dividing the No-Load Offer by
                             the Maximum Economic Capacity Operating Limit and by
                             the ratio of the number of intervals needed to meet the
                             Minimum Run Time to the number of intervals in an hour.
                2. The application of the composite begins with the commitment
                    interval and extends through the Minimum Run Time.
 (c)   In addition to dispatchable Bids and Offers, FSRs committed by the Transmission
       Provider, including FSRs committed at the request of a local transmission
       operator, but not including self-committed FSRs, will have their minimum
       operating limit relaxed to 0 MW.

 (d)   If the SPP Balancing Authority sheds load, deploys Reliability Registered
       Demand Response Programs, or requests emergency energy assistance imports
       due to a system-wide capacity issue, the net scheduled interchange and the load
       forecast used in the pricing solution will be offset according to Section 6.2.5 of
       this Attachment AE.

       For Day-Ahead Market and RTBM SCED, mitigation measures for Energy Offers
and Operating Reserve Offers, described under Sections 3.2 and 3.4 of Attachment AF of
this Tariff will be performed in the SCED pricing solution.
       An FSRs composite Energy Offer Curve will be subject to the Energy offer cap
described under Section 4.1.1 of this Attachment AE.

             Beginning seven (7) days prior to the Operating Day, Market Participants may

 4.1.2           Additional Provisions for Non-Traditional Resources

4.1.2.1            Demand Response Resources

          (1)      Dispatchable Demand Response Resource - A Dispatchable Demand Response
                   Resource is modeled in the Commercial Model the same as any other Resource,
                   except that the Settlement Location associated with the Dispatchable Demand
                   Response Resource must contain the Price Node, or aggregated Price Node as
                   described in Section 2.2(2) of this Attachment AE, associated with the Demand
                   Response Load. The Market Participant must submit the Real-Time value of the
                   Demand Response Load to the Transmission Provider via telemetering that meets
                   the technical requirements specified in the Market Protocols. The Meter Agent
                   must submit either five (5) minute or hourly actual load consumption values of
                   the Demand Response Load to the Transmission Provider. A Dispatchable
                   Demand Response Resource shall submit Energy Offer Curves based on the
                   criteria in Section 3.2(F) of Attachment AF of this Tariff. For purposes of these
                   Resources, the short-run marginal cost may equal opportunity cost.             A
                   Dispatchable Demand Response Resource may select one of two options for
                   reporting of the actual Dispatchable Demand Response Resource output:
                   (a)    Submitted Resource production option:
                          The Dispatchable Demand Response Resource output is sent directly to
                          the Transmission Provider by the Market Participant via telemetering for
                          Real-Time operational purposes and the Meter Agent submits either five
                          (5) minute or hourly actual output values to the Transmission Provider for
                          use in settlements. The submitted Resource production option is only
                          allowed for Demand Response Resources that are: (1) utilizing strictly
                          Behind-The-Meter Generation to provide the response and are utilizing
                          Real-Time metering capable of reporting both the Behind-The-Meter
                          Generation output and the load; (2) Demand Response Resources where
                          the Market Participant is offering the Resource under a retail tariff
                          provision that includes near Real-Time measurement and verification
                          terms that are compliant with the Business Practices for Measurement and
       Verification of Wholesale Electricity Demand Response of the North
      American Energy Standards Board, incorporated by reference in the
      Commission’s Regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 38.2(a)(12); or (3) Demand
      Response Load Resources utilizing near Real-Time measurement and
      verification capability that is compliant with the Business Practices for
      Measurement and Verification of Wholesale Electricity Demand Response
      of the North American Energy Standards Board, incorporated by reference
      in the Commission’s Regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 38.2(a)(12).
(b)   Calculated Resource production option:
      (i)    For each Dispatch Interval in each hour in which the Demand
             Response Resource has been committed, the Demand Response
             Resource output for Real-Time operational purposes is calculated
             by the Transmission Provider as the greater of zero (0) or the
             difference between:
             •      The lesser of the Real-Time consumption of the Demand
                    Response Load associated with the Demand Response
                    Resource in the Dispatch Interval immediately preceding
                    initial commitment of the Demand Response Resource or
                    the hourly baseline as described in (3) below for the hour,
                    and
             •      The actual value of the associated Demand Response Load
                    received via telemetering.
      (ii)   For each Dispatch Interval in each hour in which the Demand
             Response Resource has been committed, the Demand Response
             Resource output for settlement purposes is calculated by the
             Transmission Provider as the maximum of zero (0) or the
             difference between:
             •      The lesser of the Real-Time consumption of the Demand
                    Response Load associated with the Demand Response
                    Resource in the Dispatch Interval immediately preceding
                    initial commitment of the Demand Response Resource or
                              the hourly baseline as described in (3) below for the hour,
                             and
                    •        The actual value of the associated Demand Response Load
                             received from the Meter Agent either on a five (5) minute
                             basis or an hourly basis.

(2)   Block Demand Response Resource – A Block Demand Response Resource is
      modeled in the Commercial Model the same as any other Resource except that the
      Settlement Location associated with the Block Demand Response Resource must
      contain the Price Node, or aggregated Price Node as described in Section 2.2(2)
      of this Attachment AE, associated with the Demand Response Load. The Market
      Participant must submit the Real-Time value of the Demand Response Load to the
      Transmission Provider via telemetering that meets the technical requirements
      specified in the Market Protocols. All Block Demand Response Resources will
      use the calculated Resource production option, described in Section 4.1.2.1(1)(b)
      above, to determine the amount of Real-Time Resource production and actual
      Resource production.

      (a)    If the Block Demand Response Resource is committed and dispatched in
             the Day-Ahead Market, Day-Ahead RUC or Intra-Day RUC, the Block
             Demand Response Resource’s Minimum Economic Capacity Operating
             Limit will be increased in the RTBM to match the dispatched amount.
             Spinning Reserve or Supplemental Reserve will be allowed to clear above
             minimum output if the Block Demand Response Resource is a Spin
             Qualified Resource and Supplemental Reserve will be allowed to clear
             above minimum output if the Block Demand Response Resource is a
             Supplemental Qualified Resource.
      (b)    Spinning Reserve and/or Supplemental Reserve clearing will be based
             upon submitted ramp rates for the Block Demand Response Resource, the
             submitted Spinning Reserve Offer, the Supplemental Reserve Offer and
             the Block Demand Response Resource’s Maximum Economic Capacity
             Operating Limit.
(3)   Hourly Baseline
              (a)   The Market Participant must submit an hourly baseline for the Demand
                   Response Load indicating the level of energy consumption expected at
                   that location in MWh if the Demand Response Resource is not dispatched.
                   The baseline must cover, at a minimum, all hours the Resource is
                   submitting Offers for in the Energy and Operating Reserve Markets. This
                   baseline must be submitted by 1100 hours on the day prior to the
                   Operating Day and may be updated up to thirty (30) minutes in advance of
                   the operating hour. The baseline should be based on the average of the
                   hourly integrated Demand Response Load for the same hours in the last 30
                   calendar days when the Resource was not dispatched, adjusted by the
                   Market Participant as necessary to account for changes in the expected
                   level of energy consumption by the Demand Response Load.
             (b)   If there have been deviations in hourly integrated metered load from the
                   hourly baseline during periods when the Resource was not dispatched the
                   hourly baseline will be adjusted as follows by the Transmission Provider
                   prior to the calculation of the Demand Response Load. If the average of
                   the hourly deviation between integrated metered load and submitted
                   hourly baseline for the hours in the last thirty (30) calendar days when the
                   Resource was not dispatched is more than five percent (5%) below the
                   hourly baseline, the hourly baseline will be adjusted by the average
                   deviation. The Transmission Provider will perform this assessment each
                   day and notify the Market Participant of any adjustment.
             (c)   If the hourly baseline has not been submitted, the Transmission Provider
                   shall set the hourly baseline equal to the Real-Time consumption of the
                   Demand Response Load associated with the Demand Response Resource
                   in the Dispatch Interval immediately preceding initial commitment of the
                   Demand Response Resource.

4.1.2.2 Combined Cycle Resource

                   Market Participants shall select from one of the four following options
             regarding submitting Resource Offers for their registered combined cycle
 Resources, which will be declared during asset registration as described under
Sections 2.2 and 2.9 of this Attachment AE:
(1)    A Resource Offer may be submitted for a single aggregate combined cycle
       Resource, where the aggregate will represent a Market Participant selected
       operating configuration of combustion turbines and steam turbines. Under
       this option, the combined cycle Resource will be committed, dispatched
       and settled the same as any other Resource; or
(2)    A Resource Offer may be submitted for each combined cycle Resource
       combustion turbine and/or steam turbine and each component will be
       committed and dispatched independently and settled the same as any other
       single Resource; or
(3)    A Resource Offer may be submitted for each pseudo combined cycle
       Resource, where each pseudo combined cycle Resource will represent the
       combination of one combustion turbine and a portion of the steam turbine.
       Under this option, each pseudo combined cycle Resource must be capable
       of being committed and dispatched independently the same as any other
       Resource and each pseudo combined cycle Resource will be settled the
       same as any other Resource; or
(4)    A Resource Offer may be submitted for each registered combined cycle
       configuration, where each configuration represents an operating state of
       the combined cycle Resource with a distinct set of physical operating
       characteristics, as dictated by the physical attributes of the combined cycle
       Resource. Each valid configuration of an MCR will be treated as a
       separate Resource for commitment and clearing purposes. The
       Transmission Provider will determine the most economic commitment
       configuration, if requested to do so by the Market Participant as part of the
       submitted Resource Offer, and once committed, the most economic
       configuration to transition to for use in both the Day-Ahead Market and
       Real-Time Balancing Market. Settlement for a combined cycle Resource
       submitting offers in this manner will occur in the same manner as any
       other Resource except for Contingency Reserve during transitions as
                  described under Section 8.5.9 of this Attachment AE and adjustments for
                 Operating Reserves during transitions as described under Section 8.6.5 of
                 this Attachment AE. Under this option, Market Participants must define
                 during asset registration the:
                         (a)      Valid configurations, one of which must represent the
                                  maximum capacity of the combined cycle Resource;
                         (b)      Valid transitions between configurations as defined in the
                                  Market Protocols; and
                         (c)      One or more sets of physical units that can participate in a
                                  configuration.

4.1.2.3   Jointly Owned Unit

                 Under the individual Jointly Owned Unit Resource option, each Market
          Participant may submit Resource Offers for its share of the Jointly Owned Unit as
          specified in the Market Protocols. Offer parameters must meet the following
          criteria in order to be accepted as valid Offers, otherwise the last submitted valid
          offer shall apply:
          (1)    The sum of the Maximum Emergency Capacity Operating Limits of all
                 shares of the Jointly Owned Unit must be less than or equal to the Jointly
                 Owned Unit maximum physical capacity operating limit.

          Commitment of individual Jointly Owned Unit shares that have registered under
          the individual Resource option will be evaluated by security constrained unit
          commitment (“SCUC”) based on the individually submitted Offers for each
          Jointly Owned Unit share.

                 Each Market Participant may submit Resource Offers for Dispatchable

                 equal to zero;
          (2)    For the RTBM, the Resource’s Energy Offer Curve shall not apply;
          (3)    For the RTBM, the Resource’s Dispatch Instruction shall be equal to the
                 Resource’s actual output at the start of the Dispatch Interval and the
                 Resources must operate as non-dispatchable;
          (4)    Resource Energy Offer Curve prices shall be assumed equal to zero (0) for
                 the purposes of calculating production costs relating to RUC make whole
                 payments and cost allocation thereof under Sections 8.6.5 and 8.6.7 of this
                 Attachment AE;
          (5)    An OOME may be issued to a Non-Dispatchable Variable Energy
                 Resource. In addition, the Transmission Provider will issue the dispatch
                 instruction to the Resource in accordance with Section 6.2.4 of this
                 Attachment AE; and
          (6)    The maximum operating limits for use in the Day-Ahead RUC and the
                 Intra-Day RUC shall be calculated by the Transmission Provider as equal
                 to the lesser of the maximum operating limits submitted in the Resource
                 Offer or the Transmission Provider’s output forecast for that Resource to
                 the extent that such output forecast is available, otherwise the maximum
                 operating limits shall be equal to those submitted in the Resource Offer;
                 (a)     Non-Dispatchable Variable Energy Resources for which the
                         Transmission Provider is calculating an output forecast are not
                         eligible to receive RUC make whole payments as described under
                         Section 8.6.5 of this Attachment AE.
 4.1.2.6   External Dynamic Resource

          (1)    For an EDR, a Market Participant may only submit a commitment status

                 (b)     to the Real-Time Balancing Market as described in Section

2.0    Definitions


Terms defined herein shall only be applicable to this Attachment AA.


Accredited Capacity
The capacity assigned to a resource after accounting for its Conventional Resource Performance
Adjustment, Effective Load Carrying Capability Study, or Demand Response Performance
Adjustment results in accordance with this Attachment AA, SPP Planning Criteria, and SPP
Business Practices.


Accredited Capacity Planning Reserve Margin (“Accredited Capacity PRM”)
The enforceable planning reserve margin for both the Summer Season and Winter Season Pre-
Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement as determined pursuant to Section 5.0
of this Attachment AA.


Adjusted Net Peak Load
The Net Peak Load less the a) actual production output of all wind resources in the applicable SPP
Balancing Authority Area and b) actual production output of all solar resources in the applicable
SPP Balancing Authority Area.


Asset Owner
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff.


Authorized Outage
Scheduled Resource Outages which are authorized by the Balancing Authority at the time when
the Balancing Authority’s study does not identify any reliability issues with the Scheduled
Resource Outage as outlined in Section 3.1.5.1 of Attachment AE of this Tariff.


Base Planning Reserve Margin (“Base PRM”)
The planning reserve margin as determined in Section 4.0 of this Attachment AA that will be used
as the basis for calculating the Accredited Capacity PRM.
 Behind-The-Meter Generation
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff. Behind-The-Meter Generation shall not be qualified
or accredited as Demand Response Capacity in accordance with Attachment AA of this Tariff.


Conservative Operations Demand Response Program
A resource created to model Demand Response Load reduction associated with controllable load
that is 1) capable of being deployed at the direction of a Transmission Provider, Load Responsible
Entity, or a Market Participant and 2) available to respond during a) conservative operations
advisories, b) any level of EEA Emergency Conditions and c) Local Reliability Issues.


Conventional Resource Performance Adjustment
The historical performance adjustment for conventional resources using the combination of a
modified demand Equivalent Forced Outage Rate (“EFORd”) method and Equivalent Forced
Outage Factor (“EFOF”) method adjusted for Incremental Outage Impact in accordance with this
Attachment AA and the SPP Business Practices. A resource’s EFOF shall only be considered
during the Winter Season. Conventional resources are defined as thermal fuel type resources, pump
storage hydroelectric resources, and hydroelectric resources with reservoir storage capability not
subject to hourly river flow limitations similar to run-of-river hydro.


Deficiency Payment
A payment by a Market Participant when one or more of its LREs has not met the Resource
Adequacy Requirement as calculated in accordance with Section 14.0 of this Attachment AA.


Deliverable Capacity
The Accredited Capacity available for a Resource that is determined in either a Summer Season
Deliverability Study or a Winter Season Deliverability Study.


Demand Response Capacity
The Accredited Capacity of a Demand Response Resource or Reliability Registered Demand
Response Program.
 Demand Response Performance Adjustment
The historical performance adjustment for Demand Response Resource or Reliability Registered
Demand Response Program using the method(s) in accordance with this Attachment AA and the
SPP Business Practices.


Demand Response Resource
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff.


Electric Storage Resource
As defined in Part I, Section 1 of this Tariff.


Emergency Condition
As defined in Part I, Section 1 of this Tariff.


Emergency Demand Response Program
A resource created to model Demand Response Load reduction associated with controllable load
that is (1) capable of being deployed at the direction of a Transmission Provider, Load Responsible
Entity, or a Market Participant; and (2) available to respond during (a) any level of EEA
Emergency Conditions and (b) Local Reliability Issues.


Energy Emergency Alert (“EEA”)
As defined by applicable NERC Reliability Standards.


Firm Capacity
The Accredited Capacity of commercially operable generating units, or portions of generating
units, adjusted to reflect purchases and sales of capacity with another party, and that is deliverable
with firm transmission service to the LRE’s load.


Firm Power
 Power purchases and sales deliverable with firm transmission service to serve the LRE’s load with
capacity, energy, and planning reserves, that must be continuously available in a manner
comparable to power delivered to native load customers.


Firm Service Level
The expected load measured over a one clock hour period after the Demand Response Resource
or Reliability Registered Demand Response Program has been deployed to its Net Generating
Capability.


Generator Owner
The Asset Owner of a Resource.


Incremental Outage Impact
The incremental impact of simultaneous conventional resource forced outages in excess of the
normally modeled forced outages experienced during timeframes of extreme temperatures from
the LOLE Study. This value shall be assessed in accordance with the LOLE Study scope and SPP
Business Practices. Incremental Outage Impact shall only be considered during the Winter Season.


Jointly Owned Unit
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff.


Load Responsible Entity (“LRE”)
An Asset Owner with registered load in the Integrated Marketplace.


Local Reliability Issue
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff.


Market Participant
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff.


Net Generating Capability
 A resource’s gross maximum output sustained over a one-hour period, demonstrated with a
capability test, reduced by any power used for resource auxiliaries, and modified for
environmental, seasonal, operational, and fuel limitations. For resources qualified as internal to
the SPP Balancing Authority Areas, the resources shall meet the testing requirements in
accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria. Resources qualified as external to the SPP Balancing
Authority Areas shall adhere to the testing requirements of the Balancing Authority where the
resource(s) is located.


Net Peak Load
The actual Peak Demand less the actual impacts of a Demand Response Resource and Reliability
Registered Demand Response Program.


Non-Controllable and Non-Dispatchable Behind-The-Meter Generation
Behind-The-Meter Generation resources that are non-controllable and non-dispatchable by the
Transmission Provider, Market Participant, or the LRE.


Non-Registered Demand Response Program
A load reduction program that is not a Demand Response Resource or Reliability Registered
Demand Response Program.


Outage
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff.


Peak Demand
The highest demand including a) transmission losses for energy, b) the impacts of Non-
Controllable and Non-Dispatchable Behind-The-Meter Generation, and c) the impacts of Non-
Registered Demand Response Programs measured over a one clock hour period.


Post-Season Net Peak Demand
 The actual Peak Demand, normalized for weather related impacts in accordance with this
Attachment AA and SPP Business Practices, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of Firm Power
with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this Attachment AA.


Pre-Season Net Peak Demand
The forecasted Peak Demand adjusted to reflect the contract amount of Firm Power with another
entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this Attachment AA.


Pre-Season Requirement
The Pre-Season Requirement for both the Summer Season and Winter Season for each LRE is
determined pursuant to Section 5.0 of this Attachment AA.


Reliability Registered Demand Response Program (“RRDRP”)
Conservative Operations Demand Response Programs or Emergency Demand Response
Programs.


Resource
As defined in Part I, Section 1 of this Tariff.


Resource Adequacy Requirement
The Resource Adequacy Requirement for both the Summer Season and Winter Season for each
LRE is determined pursuant to Section 5.0 of this Attachment AA.


Scheduled Resource Outage
As defined in Attachment AE of this Tariff.


SPP Balancing Authority Areas
As defined in Part I, Section 1 of this Tariff.


SPP East Balancing Authority Area
As defined in Part I, Section 1 of this Tariff.
 SPP West Balancing Authority Area
As defined in Part I, Section 1 of this Tariff.


Summer Season
June 1st through September 30th of each year.


Undeployed Availability
Capacity from a Demand Response Resource or Reliability Registered Demand Response Program
available to the Transmission Provider for deployment that was not deployed as determined in
accordance with the SPP Business Practices.


Winter Season
December 1st through March 31st of each year.


Workbook
An electronic tool provided by the Transmission Provider which is used by an LRE or Generator
Owner to submit information to the Transmission Provider for the purposes of administering this
Attachment AA. The electronic tool will allow an LRE or Generator Owner to update information
contained in a previously submitted Workbook for purposes of satisfying its requirements under
Attachment AA.
 3.0   Roles and Responsibilities


3.1   Generator Owner and Load Responsible Entity
             Except as provided in Section 3.1(1) of this Attachment AA, the roles and
      responsibilities of the LRE and Generator Owner are separate and distinct from the other
      under this Attachment AA. An entity may be an LRE, a Generator Owner, or both. For
      an entity that is both an LRE and Generator Owner, the Transmission Provider shall
      recognize the rights, roles, and responsibilities as separate and distinct functions.
      (1)    An LRE that is also a Generator Owner shall access its Workbook pursuant to the
             provisions of Section 9.3(b) of this Attachment AA but shall be considered an LRE
             for Workbook reporting purposes, and all excess capacity of the Generator Owner
             shall be considered LRE Excess Capacity for purposes of Resource Adequacy
             Assurance as described in Section 14.0 of this Attachment AA.
      (2)    An entity that serves load in both the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and the
             SPP West Balancing Authority Area must separately designate the load assigned to
             the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and the load assigned to the SPP West
             Balancing Authority Area for their compliance obligations pursuant to Attachment
             AA.
      (3)    A Generator Owner that that operates Resources in both the SPP East Balancing
             Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area must separately qualify
             and assign its Resources to the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and its
             Resources to the SPP West Balancing Authority Area for their compliance
             obligations pursuant to Attachment AA.


3.2   Market Participant and Load Responsible Entity
      (1)    An LRE may be a Market Participant or can engage a third-party Market Participant
             to represent it. If an LRE refuses to either (a) become a Market Participant or (b)
             engage a third-party Market Participant to represent it, the Transmission Provider
             shall file an unexecuted Market Participant Agreement with the Commission
             pursuant to Section 2.2(6) of Attachment AE of this Tariff.
 (2)   A Market Participant that represents an LRE under Attachment AH of this Tariff is
      the entity responsible under this Attachment AA to ensure the LRE has sufficient
      capacity to meet the Pre-Season Requirement and the LRE’s compliance with the
      Resource Adequacy Requirement.
      (a)    The relationship between a Market Participant and its LRE, as established
             under Attachment AH by February 1st, will be considered fixed for the
             upcoming Summer Season for the Summer Season Pre-Season Requirement
             and enforcement of the Summer Season Resource Adequacy Requirement.

      (b)    The relationship between a Market Participant and its LRE, as established
             under Attachment AH by August 1st, will be considered fixed for the
             upcoming Winter Season for the Winter Season Pre-Season Requirement
             and enforcement of the Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement.


(3)   The Market Participant is responsible to ensure its LRE(s) provides the necessary
      data to allow the Transmission Provider to verify its LRE has sufficient capacity to
      meet the Pre-Season Requirement and its LRE(s)’ compliance with the Resource
      Adequacy Requirement.
(4)   An LRE shall submit all necessary data to the Transmission Provider either directly
      or through the LRE’s Market Participant.
(5)   A Market Participant may aggregate the forecasted Peak Demand of multiple LREs
      whose load assets are served by a common set of Designated Resources or a Firm
      Power transaction between the LREs. In such case, the Market Participant shall be
      considered the LRE for the aggregated demand and, for purposes of compliance
      with this Attachment AA, the Market Participant’s forecasted Peak Demand shall
      be used to calculate a Pre-Season Requirement and the actual Peak Demand shall
      be used to calculate a Resource Adequacy Requirement separately for the
      aggregated load assets in each SPP Balancing Authority Area.
(6)   The Market Participant is responsible for any deficient capacity for the applicable
      season’s Resource Adequacy Requirement through a Deficiency Payment incurred
      by the LRE(s) it represents.
 3.3   Procedures for Assignment of Market Participant Obligations
      (1)   A Market Participant may assign its duties, obligations and responsibilities for an
            LRE under this Attachment AA, but only to another Market Participant. A non-
            Market Participant must become a Market Participant prior to accepting an
            assignment.
      (2)   Assignor Market Participant shall be responsible to negotiate and contract with
            another Market Participant for the assignment of its duties, obligations, and
            responsibilities with respect to the LRE. A valid assignment must be in writing,
            bilaterally executed by both parties, and the assignee Market Participant shall
            affirmatively accept the duties, obligations, and responsibilities of the assignor
            Market Participant under this Attachment AA.
      (3)   For the Summer Season, the assignor Market Participant shall provide copies of the
            assignment to the Transmission Provider prior to February 1st of each calendar
            year. In the event the demonstration of such assignment does not occur prior to
            February 1st of each calendar year, the Transmission Provider shall not be required
            to accept the assignment for the upcoming Summer Season.
      (4)   For the Winter Season, the assignor Market Participant shall provide copies of the
            assignment to the Transmission Provider prior to August 1st of each calendar year.
            In the event the demonstration of such assignment does not occur prior to August
            1st of each calendar year, the Transmission Provider shall not be required to accept
            the assignment for the upcoming Winter Season.
      (5)   A valid assignment by the assignor Market Participant under this Attachment AA
            does not affect the assignor Market Participant’s status as a Market Participant or
            other rights and obligations it may have under other provisions of this Tariff.
      (6)   Except as otherwise provided in Sections 3.3(7), 3.3(8), and 3.3(9) of this
            Attachment AA, upon demonstration of a valid assignment, Transmission Provider
            will accept the transfer of the LRE to the assignee Market Participant, and enforce
            the provisions of Attachment AA against the assignee Market Participant, without
            recourse against the assignor Market Participant.
      (7)   Either party may serve the Transmission Provider with written notice of the
            assignment’s termination.      The Transmission Provider will recognize the
       assignment’s termination if the notice contains a written acknowledgement by both
      parties that the assignment has been terminated.          Upon termination of the
      assignment, the duties, obligations, and responsibilities of the Market Participant
      for the transferred LRE under Attachment AA of the Tariff shall immediately revert
      back to assignor Market Participant, unless a replacement assignment that meets
      the requirements of this section is provided to the Transmission Provider.
(8)   Nothing in the Transmission Provider’s acceptance of the assignment shall be
      construed to create or give rise to any liability on the part of the Transmission
      Provider and the parties to the assignment expressly waive any claims that may
      arise in their favor against the Transmission Provider, except as specifically may
      be provided in the Tariff. The Transmission Provider shall be held harmless by the
      parties for any breach of the assignment or dispute between the parties with regards
      to the assignment, and such dispute shall not delay or cancel the financial
      responsibilities of the assignee Market Participant under this Attachment AA. Any
      dispute between the Transmission Provider and either party may be subject to the
      dispute resolution provisions of Section 12 of the Tariff.
(9)   The Transmission Provider shall not be responsible for the actions of any party, or
      have any affirmative duties assigned to the Transmission Provider under the
      assignment. The Transmission Provider’s recognition of the assignment shall not
      be construed as Transmission Provider’s acceptance of the provisions of the
      assignment that may conflict with the Tariff or the Transmission Provider’s
      administration of the Tariff, and specifically, the application of this Attachment AA
      against the assignee Market Participant, or upon termination of the assignment, the
      assignor Market Participant. In the event there exists a conflict between a term of
      the assignment and this Tariff, the provisions of this Tariff shall control.
 5.0   Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement


5.1   The Summer Season Pre-Season Requirement is equal to the LRE’s Summer Season Pre-
      Season Net Peak Demand plus its Summer Season Pre-Season Net Peak Demand
      multiplied by the Accredited Capacity PRM for the Summer Season of the applicable SPP
      Balancing Authority Area for the LRE. The Winter Season Pre-Season Requirement is
      equal to the LRE’s Winter Season Pre-Season Net Peak Demand plus its Winter Season
      Pre-season Net Peak Demand multiplied by the Accredited Capacity PRM for the Winter
      Season of the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area for the LRE.

      (1)    The Pre-Season Net Peak Demand shall be determined by the applicable LRE or
             Market Participant and submitted in the Workbook in accordance with this
             Attachment AA.

      (2)    An LRE that resolves its capacity deficiency for the purpose of meeting the Summer
             Season Pre-Season Requirement by May 15th and resolves its capacity deficiency
             for the purpose of meeting the Winter Season Pre-Season Requirement by
             November 15th of the applicable year will be considered to have sufficient capacity
             to meet the Pre-Season Requirement.

      (3)    The LRE shall have sufficient firm transmission service from Designated
             Resources, resources associated with Firm Point-to-Point Transmission Service,
             and other resources with firm transmission service for the designated amount for
             meeting its Summer Season Pre-Season Net Peak Demand and Winter Season Pre-
             season Net Peak Demand.

5.2   The Summer Season Resource Adequacy Requirement is equal to the LRE’s Summer
      Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand plus its Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak
      Demand multiplied by the Accredited Capacity PRM for the Summer Season of the
      applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area for the LRE. The Winter Season Post-Season
      Resource Adequacy Requirement is equal to the LRE’s Winter Season Post-Season Net
      Peak Demand plus its Winter Season Net Peak Demand multiplied by the Accredited
       Capacity PRM for the Winter Season of the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area for
      the LRE.

      (1)    The Post-Season Net Peak Demand shall be determined by the Transmission
             Provider in accordance with Section 12 of this Attachment AA.

      (2)    The LRE is responsible to meet the Resource Adequacy Requirement for the
             Summer Season and Winter Season or pay for any deficiency needed to be
             compliant with the applicable year’s Resource Adequacy Requirement through a
             Deficiency Payment as calculated in accordance with Section 14.0 of this
             Attachment AA.

5.3   The Deliverable Capacity, Firm Capacity, or Demand Response Capacity utilized by an
      LRE to meet the Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement may not
      be included in the Deliverable Capacity, Firm Capacity, or Demand Response Capacity
      utilized by another LRE to meet the Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy
      Requirement. Deliverable Capacity or Firm Capacity that is contracted to other entities
      shall not be available to the LRE that is transferring the Deliverable Capacity or Firm
      Capacity for compliance with the Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy
      Requirement. Demand Response Capacity qualified to meet an LRE’s Pre-Season
      Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement shall only be available to the LRE that
      is submitting the corresponding load of the Demand Response Resource or RRDRP as Peak
      Demand in its Workbook.

      (1)    Firm Capacity qualified in accordance with this Attachment AA from Behind-The-
             Meter Generation that is not registered in the Integrated Marketplace shall have its
             capacity adjusted in determination of the Resource Adequacy Requirement in
             accordance with the SPP Business Practices when assessing the LRE’s Post Season
             Net Peak Demand.

5.4   The Transmission Provider shall use the Deliverable Capacity, Firm Capacity, Firm Power,
      or Demand Response Capacity qualified to meet an LRE’s Pre-Season Requirement to
      assess such LRE’s compliance with the Resource Adequacy Requirement.
 5.5   If an LRE serves load both internal and external to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas,
      compliance with the Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement
      contained in this Attachment AA is not intended to affect an LRE’s obligation to maintain
      distinct and separate amounts of Resources to cover its applicable planning reserve
      obligation for its load located external to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas. Load and
      Resources that are pseudo-tied or dynamically scheduled into either of the SPP Balancing
      Authority Areas shall be considered internal for purposes of determining the Pre-Season
      Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement.

5.6   The Base PRM for the Summer Season and Winter Season established in accordance with
      Section 4.0 of this Attachment AA will be used as a basis for calculating a Summer Season
      Accredited Capacity PRM and Winter Season Accredited Capacity PRM of each of the
      SPP Balancing Authority Areas by applying the Accredited Capacity for the applicable
      season in accordance with this Attachment AA and SPP Planning Criteria. The Summer
      Season Accredited Capacity PRM will be utilized to determine the Pre-Season
      Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement for the Summer Season and the Winter
      Season Accredited Capacity PRM will be utilized to determine the Pre-Season
      Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement for the Winter Season.
 6.0   Expectation of Resource Availability

            An LRE or a Generator Owner must only submit Deliverable Capacity, Firm
      Capacity, or Demand Response Capacity for the capacity of a Resource it expects will be
      available for the duration of the applicable period, which is June 15th through September
      15th for the Summer Season and December 15th through March 15th for the Winter
      Season, unless the Resource receives an Authorized Outage(s) as described in Section 11.3
      of this Attachment AA. The Balancing Authority studies Authorized Outages pursuant to
      Section 3.1.5 of Attachment AE of this Tariff. To ensure availability and readiness to
      perform, certain measures, consistent with Good Utility Practice, must be performed
      subject to the following provisions:

      (1)   The LRE must have no knowledge, consistent with Good Utility Practice, that a
            Resource included in the Workbook for meeting its Pre-Season Requirement and
            Resource Adequacy Requirement will become unavailable unless it has received an
            Authorized Outage(s) prior to inclusion in the Workbook. Unless a Resource has
            received an Authorized Outage(s), the LRE must have made reasonable efforts to
            obtain the knowledge necessary to determine whether a Resource it has included in
            the Workbook for meeting its Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy
            Requirement will become unavailable during the applicable season.

      (2)   The LRE and Generator Owner must not schedule or plan for the Resource’s
            capacity to become unavailable due to an Outage during the applicable season
            without Balancing Authority approval and authorization.

      (3)   The LRE must reflect in its Workbook any Outage that affects the Resource’s
            capacity by the Workbook submittal deadline as specified in Section 11.3 of this
            Attachment AA.

      (4)   The LRE may reflect the entire capacity of the Resource in its Workbook in order
            to meet its Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement if the
            Resource receives an Authorized Outage(s) prior to the Workbook submittal
            deadline as specified in Section 11.3 of this Attachment AA and continues to have
 the Authorized Outage(s) for the Resource on February 15th for the Summer Season
or August 15th for the Winter Season.
 7.0   Qualification of Deliverable Capacity, Firm Capacity, Firm Power, Demand
      Response Capacity, and Behind-The-Meter Generation


7.1   An LRE or Generator Owner with Deliverable Capacity from resources internal to the SPP
      Balancing Authority Areas shall qualify such capacity in the Workbook for each Summer
      Season and Winter Season by:
      (a)    registering the Resource in the Integrated Marketplace;
      (b)    submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
             Operational Test results as performed in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria;
             and
      (c)    submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
             Capability Test results as performed in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria.


7.2   An LRE or Generator Owner with Firm Capacity from a resource(s) internal to the SPP
      Balancing Authority Areas shall qualify such capacity in the Workbook for each Summer
      Season and Winter Season by:
      (a)    demonstrating the resource(s) is (i) registered in the Integrated Marketplace or (ii)
             listed as a Designated Resource in the Network Integration Transmission Service
             Agreement;
      (b)    submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
             Operational Test results as performed in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria;
      (c)    submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
             Capability Test results as performed in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria;
             and
      (d)    demonstrating that there is firm transmission service from the internal resource(s)
             to the LRE’s load.


7.3   An LRE or Generator Owner with Firm Capacity from a resource(s) external to the SPP
      Balancing Authority Areas shall qualify such capacity in the Workbook for each Summer
      Season and Winter Season by:
      (a)    demonstrating ownership or contractual rights;
       (b)    submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
             operational test results per the requirements of the Balancing Authority where the
             resource(s) is located;
      (c)    demonstrating that there is firm transmission service from the external resource(s)
             to the LRE’s load; and
      (d)    attesting that any external capacity being identified is not otherwise being used as
             capacity in any other Balancing Authority Area or in another resource adequacy
             construct.
             (1)    Resources qualified in accordance with Section 7.3 of this Attachment AA
                    shall have its Accredited Capacity determined based on the class average
                    EFORd and EFOF in accordance with Section 15.4 of this Attachment AA
                    and SPP Business Practices if no historical performance data is provided to
                    the Transmission Provider.


7.4   An LRE with Firm Power from a resource(s) internal to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas
      shall qualify those purchases or sales in the Workbook for each Summer Season and Winter
      Season by:
      (a)    demonstrating the resource(s) is: (i) registered in the Integrated Marketplace; or (ii)
             listed as a Designated Resource in the Network Integration Transmission Service
             Agreement;
      (b)    submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
             Operational Test results as performed in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria;
      (c)    submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
             Capability Test results as performed in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria;
             and
      (d)    demonstrating that there is firm transmission service from the internal resource(s)
             to the LRE’s load.


7.5   An LRE with Firm Power from a resource(s) external to the SPP Balancing Authority
      Areas shall qualify those purchases or sales in the Workbook for each Summer Season and
      Winter Season by:
       (a)   demonstrating ownership or contractual rights;
      (b)   submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
            operational test results per the requirements of the Balancing Authority where the
            resource(s) is located;
      (c)   demonstrating that there is firm transmission service from the external resource(s)
            to the LRE’s load;
      (d)   demonstrating that the capacity includes planning reserves; and
      (e)   attesting that any external capacity being identified is not otherwise being used as
            capacity in any other Balancing Authority Area or in another resource adequacy
            construct.
            (1)     Resources qualified in accordance with Section 7.5 of this Attachment AA
                    shall have its Accredited Capacity determined based on the class average
                    EFORd and EFOF in accordance with Section 15.4 of this Attachment AA
                    and SPP Business Practices if no historical performance data is provided to
                    the Transmission Provider.


7.6   An LRE claiming Firm Capacity from Behind-The-Meter Generation less than 10 MW
      internal to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas shall qualify such generation in the
      Workbook for each Summer Season and Winter Season by:
      (a)   acknowledging it is controlled or dispatched by an LRE or Market Participant;
      (b)   submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the
            appropriate reporting and documentation requirements in accordance with the SPP
            Business Practices;
      (c)   submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current
            Operational Test results as performed in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria;
      (d)   submitting, or causing to be submitted, to the Transmission Provider the current

 8.0   Qualification and Verification of Power Purchase Agreements



8.1   An LRE or Generator Owner shall provide the Transmission Provider a copy of the power
      purchase agreement(s) to enable the Transmission Provider to verify the Deliverable
      Capacity, Firm Capacity, or Firm Power and to confirm compliance with this Attachment
      AA. On a prospective basis, the LRE or Generator Owner shall only submit a copy of a
      new or modified agreement(s).

      (1)    Any redacted versions of a power purchase agreement submitted by an LRE or
             Generator Owner shall contain sufficient information to allow the Transmission
             Provider to verify sufficiency with the Pre-Season Requirement and compliance
             with the Resource Adequacy Requirement.

      (2)    An LRE or Generator Owner with a power purchase agreement that does not
             identify the specific resource(s) shall identify each resource that is available or
             partially available through an attestation supporting the power purchase agreement.
      (3)    A power purchase agreement used to meet the Pre-Season Requirement and
             Resource Adequacy Requirement shall be limited to the Accredited Capacity of the
             resource(s) identified in the power purchase agreement or identified in accordance
             with Section 8.1 of this Attachment AA.


8.2   When the purchaser and seller are both LREs, a power purchase agreement that qualifies
      as Firm Power shall result in a Pre-Season Net Peak Demand and Post-Season Net Peak
      Demand adjustment of the obligation for capacity and planning reserves from the purchaser
      to the seller. The purchaser shall deduct the purchased contract amount from its Pre-Season
      Net Peak Demand and the seller shall add the amount to its Pre-Season Net Peak Demand.
      Likewise, the Transmission Provider shall deduct the purchased contract amount from the
      purchaser’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand and shall add the amount to the seller’s Post-
      Season Net Peak Demand. The responsibility to maintain the Pre-Season Requirement and
      Resource Adequacy Requirement shall transfer from the purchaser to the seller.
 8.3   When the seller is not an LRE, a power purchase agreement that qualifies as Firm Power
      shall not result in a Pre-Season Net Peak Demand and Post-Season Net Peak Demand
      adjustment and the purchaser will remain responsible for the Pre-Season Requirement and
      Resource Adequacy Requirement for load served by the agreement. The purchaser shall
      not deduct the purchased contract amount from its Pre-Season Net Peak Demand; however,
      the purchaser may reflect as Firm Capacity the contract amount of the agreement plus the
      purchaser’s Accredited Capacity PRM for the applicable season multiplied by the contract
      amount. Likewise, the Transmission Provider shall not adjust the purchaser’s Post-Season
      Net Peak Demand for the contracted amount. Firm transmission service is only required
      for the contract amount.


8.4   When the purchaser is not an LRE, a power purchase agreement that qualifies as Firm
      Power shall result in a Firm Capacity transaction for load served by the agreement. The
      seller, who is an LRE, shall not include the purchased contract amount in its Pre-Season
      Net Peak Demand; however, the seller shall reflect as Firm Capacity the contract amount
      of the agreement plus the seller’s Accredited Capacity PRM for the applicable season
      multiplied by the contract amount. Likewise, the Transmission Provider shall not adjust
      the seller’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand for the contracted amount. Firm transmission
      service is only required for the contract amount.


8.5   A power purchase agreement executed prior to July 1, 2018 will continue to be defined and
      qualified as Firm Power if it does not include provisions permitting the seller to interrupt
      deliveries thereunder for reasons other than Force Majeure (as defined in Section 10.1 of
      this Tariff) or uncured defaults. All other power purchase agreements must specifically
      meet the definition of Firm Power.


8.6   An LRE may arrange for short-term capacity to provide a part of its Firm Capacity or short-
      term Firm Power to reduce a portion of its Pre-Season Net Peak Demand or Post-Season
      Net Peak Demand for the Summer Season or Winter Season, subject to the following
      provisions:
       (1)    Such short-term capacity or short-term Firm Power shall be available for a
             minimum of four consecutive months, starting either June 1st or December 1st;
      (2)    The amount of short-term Firm Capacity or short-term Firm Power purchased in
             aggregate shall not exceed 25% of an LRE’s applicable Pre-Season Net Peak
             Demand and Post-Season Net Peak Demand; and
      (3)    If the seller under a short-term Firm Power agreement is not an LRE, then the
             purchaser under the short-term Firm Power agreement will remain responsible for
             any Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement for load
             served under the short-term Firm Power agreement.
