 10.0   Deliverability Study


10.1   The Transmission Provider shall perform a Deliverability Study for the Summer Season
       and a Deliverability Study for the Winter Season every year. There will be a separate
       Deliverability Study each season for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and the SPP
       West Balancing Authority Area. The Deliverability Study for the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area will study the following: (1)
       whether a Resource is deliverable to load located within the same SPP Balancing Authority
       Area; and (2) whether the Resource is deliverable to load located in the SPP Balancing
       Authority Area where the Resource is not located. Each Deliverability Study will evaluate
       each Resource registered in the Integrated Marketplace to determine the Deliverable
       Capacity each Resource has to load located within both the SPP Balancing Authority Area
       where the Resource is located and to the SPP Balancing Authority Area where the Resource
       is not located. To determine the Resource’s seasonal capacity that is deliverable to load
       located within the SPP Balancing Authority Area where the Resource is located, the
       Transmission Provider will determine each Resource’s deliverable amount that is
       deliverable to load in the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area and not whether a
       particular Resource is deliverable to specific delivery points or SPP Zones. To determine
       a Resource’s seasonal capacity that is deliverable to load located within the SPP Balancing
       Authority Area where the Resource is not located, the Transmission Provider will
       determine the Deliverable Capacity amount of each Resource in the same SPP Balancing
       Authority Area by studying the deliverability of all Resources to the aggregate interface of
       the West DC Ties and determine a Deliverable Capacity amount of each Resource by
       studying the deliverability from the aggregate interface of the West DC Ties to the SPP
       Balancing Authority Area where the Resource is not located. For a Resource to have
       seasonal capacity that is deliverable to load located in a SPP Balancing Authority Area in
       which a Resource is not located, the Resource shall be limited to the lesser of the following:
       (1) the Resource’s MW amounts deliverable to the aggregate interface of the West DC
       Ties; (2) the Resource’s MW amounts from the aggregate interface of West DC Ties to the
       SPP Balancing Authority Area in which the Resource is not located, and (3) the firm
       Transmission Service capacity across the West DC Tie that has been reserved for the
        entirety of the applicable season. A Resource’s Deliverable Capacity amount for an
       applicable season is limited to the amount of Deliverable Capacity available to the SPP
       Balancing Authority Area in which the Resource is located plus the amount of Deliverable
       Capacity available to the SPP Balancing Authority Area in which the Resource is not
       located, but cannot exceed the total Net Generating Capacity of the Resource. The results
       of the Summer Season Deliverability Study shall be valid for the upcoming Summer
       Season and the subsequent Summer Season.             The results of the Winter Season
       Deliverability Study shall be valid for the upcoming Winter Season and the subsequent
       Winter Season.


10.2   The Transmission Provider will utilize its current transmission planning models to perform
       the Summer Season Deliverability Study and the Winter Season Deliverability Study. The
       Transmission Provider will begin each Deliverability Study with the initial assumption that
       any Resource generating in the planning model is automatically deliverable to the SPP
       Balancing Authority Areas for which the Resource being studied resides for the dispatched
       output. A Resource’s total capacity equals the generating unit’s maximum output of MWs.
       For multiple generating units at one site, the total capacity for the site is the sum of
       maximum MWs of all generating units. A transfer level equal to the difference between
       the Resource’s maximum MW capacity and the amount dispatched in the planning model
       is determined for each Resource. Each transfer will consist of at least one Resource or may
       consist of multiple Resources grouped together, as specified in either the Summer Season
       Deliverability Study or the Winter Season Deliverability Study scope. A First Contingency
       Incremental Transfer Capability (“FCITC”) analysis of each transfer will be performed to
       determine the deliverability of the Resource. Transmission Facilities 100 kV and above
       will be included in the FCITC analysis. A three percent (3%) transfer distribution factor
       threshold will be used to analyze constraints impacted by the transfer.


10.3   The Summer Season Deliverability Study and the Winter Season Deliverability Study
       results for each Generator Owner’s Resource to the SPP Balancing Authority Area for
       which it is located shall consist of the total Resource’s deliverability of MW amounts to
       that SPP Balancing Authority Area. Each Generator Owner of a Jointly Owned Unit will
        coordinate to determine the MW deliverability amounts for its share of a Jointly Owned
       Unit.
       10.3.1 The Summer Season Deliverability Study and the Winter Season Deliverability
               Study results for each Generator Owner’s Resource that determines deliverability
               of capacity of the Resource to the a SPP Balancing Authority Area where the
               Resource is not located shall be limited to the lesser of the following: (1) the
               Resource’s MW amounts deliverable to the aggregate interface of the West DC
               Ties, (2) the Resource’s MW amounts from the aggregate interface of West DC
               Ties to the SPP Balancing Authority Area for which the Resource is not located,
               and (3) the firm Transmission Service capacity across the West DC Tie that has
               been reserved for the entirety of the applicable season.
       10.3.2 The availability of transmission service rights to the West DC Tie is not conveyed
               by the Deliverability Study.

10.4   The amount of Deliverable Capacity of any Resource available for purchase to meet the
       Pre-Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement shall equal the lesser of: a)
       the Resource’s Accredited Capacity less the MW amount of capacity that has been
       committed to meet for the applicable season i) Firm Capacity and ii) a sale to another entity;
       or b) the amount of a Resource’s total deliverable MWs less the MW amount of capacity
       that has been committed to meet for the applicable season i) Firm Capacity and ii) a sale to
       another entity, as determined from the Generator Owner’s Workbook.


10.5   A Generator Owner that does not submit or update a Workbook to the Transmission
       Provider by May 15th for the Summer Season or by November 15th for the Winter Season
       that contains the amount of generation capacity available through each Deliverability Study
       shall be deemed to have no Deliverable Capacity that shall not be entitled to receive any
       revenue distributions collected from Deficiency Payments.


10.6   Demand Response Resource(s) or RRDRP(s) shall not be a) eligible to be used as
       Deliverable Capacity and b) available for purchase to satisfy the Pre-Season Requirement
       and Resource Adequacy Requirement.
 10.7   A power purchase agreement to satisfy the Pre-Season Requirement and Resource
       Adequacy Requirement based on the most recent Summer Season or Winter Season
       Deliverability Study may only rely on the results of such study for no longer than the
       upcoming Summer Season or Winter Season and the subsequent Summer Season or Winter
       Season.
       (1)    Deliverable Capacity purchases by an LRE to satisfy the Resource Adequacy
              Requirement will not require firm transmission service to support the capacity.
              Deliverable Capacity purchases shall not entitle a Market Participant to receive
              Auction Revenue Rights under Attachment AE of the Tariff.
 11.0   Workbook


11.1   The Generator Owner’s Workbook for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season
       will contain, but is not limited to, the following information:
       (1)    Capacity owned by the Generator Owner;
       (2)    Capacity sales to another entity; and
       (3)    Uncommitted Deliverable Capacity.


11.2   The LRE’s Workbook for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season will contain,
       but is not limited to, the following information:
       (1)    The LRE’s Summer Season or Winter Season Net Peak Demand;
       (2)    Capacity owned by the LRE;
       (3)    Purchases and sales for Deliverable Capacity:
       (4)    Purchases and sales for Firm Capacity;
       (5)    Purchases and sales for Firm Power;
       (6)    Uncommitted Deliverable Capacity;
       (7)    Demand Response Capacity;
       (8)    Projected amount from Non-Registered Demand Response Programs included in
              the Peak Demand; and
       (9)    Most recent load forecasting methodology materials as required in the SPP
              Business Practices.


11.3   The LRE’s Workbook for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season shall be subject
       to the following provisions:

       (1)    A Workbook will be used to qualify the LRE’s compliance with the Pre-Season
              Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement for the upcoming Summer
              Season or Winter Season.        Absent a calculation error or otherwise incorrect
              information, an LRE that demonstrates compliance with the requirements of
              Section 5.0 of this Attachment AA is considered to have met its Pre-Season
       Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement, subject to any subsequently
      reported sales.

      (a)    An LRE shall update its Workbook by May 15th for the Summer Season to
             correct calculation errors or incorrect information.

      (b)    An LRE shall update its Workbook by November 15th for the Winter
             Season to correct calculation errors or incorrect information.

(2)   A Workbook for the Summer Season may include any Resources, provided the
      Resource’s capacity is expected to be available for the duration of June 15th through
      September 15th.

      (a)    In the event a Resource receives an Authorized Outage(s) prior to the
             February 15th and the aggregated timeframe for all Authorized Outages of
             that Resource does not exceed 30 calendar days during the applicable
             period, the entire Resource’s capacity may be included in the Workbook.

      (b)    After February 15th, if the expected availability of a Resource changes to
             unavailable during June 15th through September 15th, the Resource will be
             considered as available for purposes of meeting the Summer Season Pre-
             Season Requirement and Resource Adequacy Requirement.               Capacity
             cannot be purchased from Resources after the capacity of the Resource
             becomes unavailable. Resources that were not initially submitted in the
             Workbook by February 1st but are later submitted in the updated Workbook
             prior to May 15th must have an expectation of availability in accordance
             with Section 6.0 of this Attachment AA at the time the Resource is
             submitted in the updated Workbook.

      (c)    Should a Resource that is initially identified in the Workbook to be
             unavailable but subsequently becomes available or has, an expectation of
             availability in accordance with Section 6.0 of this Attachment AA at the
             time the Resource is submitted in the Workbook, and the LRE updates the
             Workbook by May 15th, such Resource will count as capacity for purposes
              of meeting the Summer Season Pre-Season Requirement and Resource
             Adequacy Requirement.

(3)   A Workbook for the Winter Season may include any Resources, provided the
      Resource’s capacity is expected to be available for the duration of December 15th
      through March 15th.

      (a)    In the event a Resource receives an Authorized Outage(s) prior to the
             August 15th and the aggregated timeframe for all Authorized Outages of
             that Resource does not exceed 30 calendar days during the applicable
             period, the entire Resource’s capacity may be included in the Workbook.

      (b)    After August 15th, if the expected availability of a Resource changes to
             unavailable during December 15th through March 15th, the Resource will
             be considered as available for purposes of meeting the Winter Season
             Resource Adequacy Requirement. Capacity cannot be purchased from
             Resources after the capacity of the Resource becomes unavailable.
             Resources that were not initially submitted in the Workbook by August 1st
             but are later submitted in the updated Workbook prior to November 15th
             must have an expectation of availability in accordance with Section 6.0 of
             this Attachment AA at the time the Resource is submitted in the updated
             Workbook.

      (c)    Should a Resource that is initially identified in the Workbook to be
             unavailable but subsequently becomes available or has, an expectation of
             availability in accordance with Section 6.0 of this Attachment AA at the
             time the Resource is submitted in the Workbook, and the LRE updates the
             Workbook by November 15th, such Resource will count as capacity for
             purposes of meeting the Winter Season Pre-Season Requirement and
             Resource Adequacy Requirement.
 12.0   Post-Season Net Peak Demand

12.1   The actual Peak Demand shall be adjusted by weather normalization based on the
       individual LRE’s forecasting practices to determine the Post-Season Net Peak Demand.
       The Transmission Provider shall apply the weather normalization process, and additional
       adjustments necessary to determine the Post-Season Net Peak Demand, in accordance with
       the SPP Business Practices.

12.2   Any impact to an LRE’s actual Peak Demand from a Demand Response Resource or
       RRDRP, for which the LRE has qualified for the applicable season, shall be summed
       together and added to the applicable LRE’s actual Peak Demand hour when determining
       the actual LRE’s actual Peak Demand in accordance with the SPP Business Practices.

       (1)    In the event the actual metered load for the applicable interval is less than the Firm
              Service Level, the Demand Response Capacity of such resources shall be added
              back to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand for that same hour.

       (2)    In the event the actual metered load for the applicable interval is greater than the
              Firm Service Level, but less than the Net Generating Capacity plus the Firm Service
              Level, the amount added back to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand for that same hour
              shall be calculated as follows:

              Net Generating Capability + Firm Service Level - actual metered load

       (3)    In the event the actual metered load for the applicable interval is greater than the
              Net Generating Capacity plus the Firm Service Level, no amount shall be added
              back to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand for that same hour.

12.3   In the event the LRE or Market Participant has not submitted in the Workbook the load
       forecasting methodology materials as outlined in the SPP Business Practices, the
       Transmission Provider shall apply a default methodology to normalize the LRE actual Net
       Peak Demand for weather related impacts the LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand for
       the applicable season.
 14.0   Resource Adequacy Assurance


14.1   Variables

       The variables used in the calculations are as follows:
       (1)    Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              The available Deliverable Capacity above the committed capacity of Generator
              Owner Resource(s) in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area as reflected in its
              completed Workbook.        Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP East
              Balancing Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season Resource
              Adequacy Requirement and the Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement.
       (2)    Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
              The available Deliverable Capacity above the committed capacity of Generator
              Owner Resource(s) in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area as reflected in its
              completed Workbook. Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP West
              Balancing Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season Resource
              Adequacy Requirement and the Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement.
       (3)    LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              The Transmission Provider will determine LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East
              Balancing Authority Area for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season. The
              Transmission Provider will determine the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East
              Balancing Authority Area as follows:
              (a)     In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is less than or
                      equal to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract
                      amount of Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
                      Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
                      Authority Area shall be:
                      (i)     the Resource Adequacy Requirement of an LRE in the SPP East
                              Balancing Authority Area less the sum of Deliverable Capacity,
                              Demand Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE;
                              or
              (ii)    zero, if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                     Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is greater than or
                     equal to the Resource Adequacy Requirement of the same LRE.
      (b)    In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is greater than
             the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
             Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
             Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
             Authority Area shall be:
             (i)     the actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
                     Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
                     Attachment AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity
                     PRM for the applicable season of the SPP East Balancing Authority
                     Area) less the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                     Capacity, and Firm Capacity; or
              (ii)   zero, if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                     Capacity, and Firm Capacity is greater than or equal to the actual
                     Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of Firm Power
                     with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this Attachment
                     AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity PRM for the
                     applicable season of the SPP East Balancing Authority Area).
(4)   LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
      The Transmission Provider will determine LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP
      West Balancing Authority Area for both the Summer Season and the Winter
      Season. The Transmission Provider will determine the LRE Deficient Capacity for
      the SPP West Balancing Authority Area as follows:
      (a)    In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is less than or
             equal to the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract
             amount of Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
             Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing
             Authority Area shall be:
              (i)    the Resource Adequacy Requirement of an LRE in the SPP West
                    Balancing Authority Area less the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand
                    Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE; or

             (ii)   zero if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                    Capacity, and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is greater than or
                    equal to the Resource Adequacy Requirement of the same LRE.
      (b)    In the event that an LRE’s Post-Season Net Peak Demand is greater than
             the LRE’s actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
             Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
             Attachment AA, the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing
             Authority Area shall be:
              (i)   the actual Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of
                    Firm Power with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this
                    Attachment AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity
                    PRM for the applicable season of the SPP West Balancing Authority
                    Area) less the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                    Capacity, and Firm Capacity; or
             (ii)   zero, if the sum of Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
                    Capacity, and Firm Capacity is greater than or equal to the actual
                    Peak Demand, adjusted to reflect the contract amount of Firm Power
                    with another entity as specified in Section 8.2 of this Attachment
                    AA, multiplied by (one plus the Accredited Capacity PRM for the
                    applicable season of the SPP West Balancing Authority Area).
(5)   LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
      Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of an LRE
      in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area less Resource Adequacy Requirement of
      the same LRE, or zero if the Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response Capacity,
      and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is less than or equal to the Resource Adequacy
      Requirement of the same LRE. LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing
      Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season.
(6)   LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response Capacity, and Firm Capacity of an LRE
      in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area less Resource Adequacy Requirement
      of the same LRE, or zero if the Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response Capacity,
      and Firm Capacity of the same LRE is less than or equal to the Resource Adequacy
      Requirement of the same LRE. LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP West Balancing
      Authority Area is determined for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season.
(7)   SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning Reserve
      Summer Season = [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
      Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area less the sum
      of all LREs’ Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP East
      Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess Capacity
      for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all LREs’
      Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP East Balancing
      Authority Area.
      Winter Season = [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
      Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area less the sum
      of all LREs’ Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP East
      Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess Capacity
      for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all LREs’ Winter
      Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP East Balancing Authority Area.
(8)   SPP West Balancing Authority Area Planning Reserve
      Summer Season = [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
      Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area less the
      sum of all LREs’ Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP West
      Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess Capacity
      for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all LREs’
      Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP West Balancing
      Authority Area.
      Winter Season = [(The sum of all LREs’ Deliverable Capacity, Demand Response
      Capacity, and Firm Capacity in the SPP West Balancing Authority Area less the
      sum of all LREs’ Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP West
        Balancing Authority Area) plus the sum of all Generator Owner Excess Capacity
       for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area] divided by the sum of all LREs’
       Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand in the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area.
(9)    Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       A piecewise curve defined by four linear functions assessing the value of excess
       Accredited Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area based on the
       relative magnitude of Accredited Capacity to the sum of all LREs’ Resource
       Adequacy Requirement for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area.
(10)   Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       A piecewise curve defined by four linear functions assessing the value of excess
       Accredited Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area based on the
       relative magnitude of Accredited Capacity to the sum of all LREs’ Resource
       Adequacy Requirement for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.
(11)   Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       The intersection of the Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the Regional Accredited Value for the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area for the applicable Winter Season or Summer Season.
(12)   Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       The intersection of the Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area and the Regional Accredited Value for the SPP West Balancing
       Authority Area for the applicable Winter Season or Summer Season.
(13)   Regional Accredited Value for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       The total Accredited Capacity to meet the Resource Adequacy Requirement for the
       SPP East Balancing Authority Area plus the Generator Owned Excess Capacity for
       the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East
       Balancing Authority Area.
(14)   Regional Accredited Value for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
       The total Accredited Capacity to meet the Resource Adequacy Requirement for the
       SPP West Balancing Authority Area plus the Generator Owned Excess Capacity
               for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area and LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP
              West Balancing Authority Area.
       (15)   Sufficiency Charge for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area multiplied by
              the Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP East Balancing Authority
              Area.
       (16)   Sufficiency Charge for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
              LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area multiplied by
              the Sufficiency Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP West Balancing Authority
              Area.
       (17)   Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              A pro rata allocation of Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP East
              Balancing Authority Area, as described in Section 14.5 of this Attachment AA,
              used to resolve any LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
              Area.
       (18)   Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
              A pro rata allocation of Generator Owner Excess Capacity for the SPP West
              Balancing Authority Area, as described in Section 14.6 of this Attachment AA,
              used to resolve any LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority
              Area.
       (19)   LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
              A pro rata allocation of LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
              Area, as described in Section 14.5 of this Attachment AA, used to resolve any LRE
              Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area.
       (20)   LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area
              A pro rata allocation of LRE Excess Capacity for the SPP West Balancing
              Authority Area, as described in Section 14.6 of this Attachment AA, used to resolve
              any LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP West Balancing Authority Area.
14.2   Deficiency Payment for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area

       (1)    The Deficiency Payment shall be calculated using the applicable CONE and CONE
              Factor for both the Summer Season and Winter Season and the amount of LRE
 Deficient Capacity for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season. The
Deficiency Payment shall only be assessed for the Resource Adequacy
Requirement and will not be assessed for the Pre-Season Requirement. The
Deficiency Payment assessed to the LRE shall reflect the seasonal deficiency
quantity and the seasonal reliability need set by the CONE Factor for both seasons
as described below:
       Deficiency Payment = Greater of the Winter Season Deficiency Amount
       and the Summer Season Deficiency Amount for the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area
(a)    Summer Season Deficiency Amount for the SPP East Balancing Authority
       Area = [LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       * CONE * CONE FACTOR for the Summer Season Resource Adequacy
       Requirement for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area]

(b)    Winter Season Deficiency Amount for the SPP East Balancing Authority
       Area = [LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
       * CONE * CONE FACTOR for the Winter Season Resource Adequacy
       Requirement for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area]

(c)    The CONE FACTOR for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area shall be
       determined individually for both the Summer Season and the Winter Season
       as follows:

       (i)     125% when the SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning
               Reserve is greater than or equal to the Accredited Capacity PRM for
               the applicable season plus 8%; or
       (ii)    150% when the SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning
               Reserve is greater than or equal to the Accredited Capacity PRM for
               the applicable season plus 3%, but less than the Accredited Capacity
               PRM for the applicable season plus 8%; or
       (iii)   200% when the SPP East Balancing Authority Area Planning
               Reserve is less than the Accredited Capacity PRM for the applicable
               season plus 3%.
 (d)   An LRE that fails to meet the Summer Season Resource Adequacy
      Requirement of the applicable year or fails to meet the Winter Season
      Resource Adequacy Requirement of the applicable year shall be subject to
      the Deficiency Payment for any deficient capacity needed by an LRE to be
      sufficient for the applicable Summer Season Resource Adequacy
      Requirement or Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement. An LRE
      will be sufficient for the Summer Season Resource Adequacy Requirement
      and Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement with its payment of
      the Deficiency Payment.

(e)   A Market Participant, or its LRE, that does not submit the Workbook to the
      Transmission Provider by May 15th of the applicable year for the Summer
      Season Resource Adequacy Requirement will be considered one hundred
      percent (100%) deficient of the Pre-Season Requirement and in violation of
      the Resource Adequacy Requirement for the upcoming Summer Season and
      shall subject the responsible Market Participant to the Deficiency Payment
      for the entire Summer Season Resource Adequacy Requirement. A Market
      Participant, or its LRE, that does not submit the Workbook to the
      Transmission Provider by November 15th of the applicable year for the
      Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement will be considered one
      hundred percent (100%) deficient of the Pre-Season Requirement and in
      violation of the Resource Adequacy Requirement for the upcoming Winter
      Season and shall subject the responsible Market Participant to the
      Deficiency Payment for the entire Winter Season Resource Adequacy
      Requirement. To calculate the LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East
      Balancing Authority Area for the Summer Season Resource Adequacy
      Requirement, the Transmission Provider shall set the Deliverable Capacity,
      Firm Capacity, and Demand Response Capacity to zero and utilize the
      previous year’s applicable Summer Season Peak Demand. To calculate the
      LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area for the
      Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement, the Transmission
      Provider shall set the Deliverable Capacity, Firm Capacity, and Demand
              Response Capacity to zero and utilize the previous year’s applicable Winter
             Season Peak Demand.

      (f)    LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and
             Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority
             Area must not be contracted to any other entity internal or external to the
             SPP Balancing Authority Areas at any point during the applicable Summer
             Season for the revenue distribution as described in Section 14.5 of this
             Attachment AA. Within seven (7) Business Days after May 15th, the
             Transmission Provider shall notify LREs or Generator Owners the amount
             LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and
             Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority
             Area that shall not be subsequently contracted to any other entity internal or
             external to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas at any point during the
             applicable Summer Season.
      (g)    LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and
             Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority
             Area must not be contracted to any other entity internal or external to the
             SPP Balancing Authority Areas at any point during the applicable Winter
             Season for the revenue distribution as described in Section 14.5 of this
             Attachment AA. Within seven (7) Business Days after November 15th, the
             Transmission Provider shall notify LREs or Generator Owners the amount
             LRE Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and
             Generator Owner Capacity Allocation for the SPP East Balancing Authority
             Area that shall not be subsequently contracted to any other entity internal or
             external to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas at any point during the
             applicable Winter Season.
(2)   LREs will be subject the following Deficiency Payment based on the Sufficiency
      Valuation Curve for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area, instead of the
      Deficiency Payment described in Section 14.2(1) of this Attachment AA, for the
      2026, 2027, 2028 Summer Season Resource Adequacy Requirement and the 2026-
      2027, 2027-2028, and 2028-2029 Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement
 and, anytime thereafter for the following two Summer Season Resource Adequacy
Requirements (if applicable) and the following two Winter Season Resource
Adequacy Requirements (if applicable) after a Base PRM increase for the
applicable season for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area, based on the results
of the LOLE study, is approved by the Regional State Committee and the SPP
Board of Directors starting with the planning year for which the change in the Base
PRM will apply, provided the following: (i) the LRE had not contracted to sell
capacity to another entity external to one or both of the SPP Balancing Authority
Areas after the approval of the Base PRM change for the applicable season and had
not met the Pre-Season Requirement for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area for
either the Summer Season or the Winter Season; and (ii) LRE has demonstrated
adequate capacity to meet the current applicable Summer Season Pre-Season
Requirement and Winter Season Pre-Season Requirement for the applicable season
in effect prior to the increase approved by the SPP Board of Directors. The
Deficiency Payment based on the Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP East
Balancing Authority Area shall be calculated for both the Summer Season and
Winter Season. The Summer Season Deficiency Payment will be based on the LRE
Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand and the LRE's Summer Season
Resource Adequacy Requirement; the Winter Season Deficiency Payment will be
based on the LRE Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak Demand and the LRE's
Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement. The Deficiency Payment
assessed to the LRE shall reflect the seasonal deficiency quantity and the seasonal
reliability need set by for both seasons as described below:
(a)    Deficiency Payment based on the Sufficiency Valuation Curve for the SPP
       East Balancing Authority Area = Greater of the Sufficiency Valuation
       Deficiency Amount for the Summer Season or the Sufficiency Valuation
       Deficiency Amount for the Winter Season
       (i)     Sufficiency Valuation Deficiency Amount for the Summer Season
               = LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority
               Area for the Summer Season multiplied by the Sufficiency
         Valuation Clearing Price for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
        for the Summer Season.
(ii)    Sufficiency Valuation Deficiency Amount for the Winter Season =
        LRE Deficient Capacity for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
        for the Winter Season multiplied by the Sufficiency Valuation
        Clearing Price for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area for the
        Winter Season.
(iii)   Sufficiency Valuation Curve Amount for the SPP East Balancing
        Authority Area for the Summer Season and Sufficiency Valuation
        Curve Amount for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area for the
        Winter Season is defined piecewise as:
        (a)    200% CONE when the Regional Accredited Value for the
               SPP East Balancing Authority Area is less than or equal to
               the sum of all LREs’ Summer Season Post-Season Net Peak
               Demand for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area for the
               Summer Season Resource Adequacy Requirement or the
               sum of all LREs’ Winter Season Post-Season Net Peak
               Demand for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area for the
               Winter Season Resource Adequacy Requirement;
        (b)    Net CONE when the Regional Accredited Value for the SPP
               East Balancing Authority Area for the Summer Season when
               calculating the Deficiency Payment for the Summer Season
               Resource    Adequacy    Requirement    or   the   Regional
               Accredited Value for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
               for the Winter Season when calculating the Deficiency
               Payment for the Winter Season Resource Adequacy
               Requirement equals the sum of all LREs’ Resource
               Adequacy Requirement for the SPP East Balancing
               Authority Area for the applicable Summer Season or Winter
               Season;
 (c)   $0 when the Regional Accredited Value for the SPP East
      Balancing Authority Area for the Summer Season when
      calculating the Deficiency Payment for the Summer Season
      Resource    Adequacy     Requirement     or   the   Regional
      Accredited Value for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
      for the Winter Season when calculating the Deficiency
      Payment for the Winter Season Resource Adequacy
      Requirement equals or exceeds [100% plus the Accredited
      Capacity PRM for the applicable season] times the sum of
      all LREs’ Resource Adequacy Requirement for the SPP East
      Balancing Authority Area for the applicable Summer Season

14.4   Billing Procedure

              On an annual basis, the Transmission Provider shall calculate the Deficiency
       Payment amounts to be assessed against a Market Participant in the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area pursuant to Section 14.2 and
       Section 14.3 of this Attachment AA needed by the LRE to be sufficient for the applicable
       season’s Resource Adequacy Requirement. On or before September 1st of the year after
        the applicable calendar year, the Transmission Provider shall submit an invoice to the
       Market Participant as a charge for the Deficiency Payment amount. The invoice shall be
       paid by the Market Participant within seven (7) calendar days of receipt. All payments
       shall be made in immediately available funds payable to the Transmission Provider, or by
       wire transfer to a bank named by the Transmission Provider. In the event of a dispute
       between the Transmission Provider and the Market Participant related to the calculation
       and assessment of a Deficiency Payment, the Market Participant shall pay the amount in
       dispute, and the Transmission Provider shall deposit into an escrow account the portion of
       the invoice in dispute, pending resolution of such dispute.

 15.0   Accredited Capacity


15.1   Effective Load Carrying Capability Study for Wind, Solar, and Energy Storage
       Resources
       (1)   Capacity accreditation for wind resources, solar resources, and Energy Storage
             Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources, will be established
             using an Effective Load Carrying Capability (“ELCC”) Study, as described in
             Section 15.1 of this Attachment AA, SPP Business Practices and SPP Planning
             Criteria. The ELCC Study for capacity accreditation of wind resources, solar
             resources, and Energy Storage Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric
             resources, shall be conducted separately for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area
             and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area based on which SPP Balancing
             Authority Area those Resources are located. When the term “load” is used in this
             Section 15, it is understood that the term refers to the load of the applicable SPP
             Balancing Authority Area in which the Resources being evaluated are located. The
             ELCC Study for each resource type will consist of probabilistic analyses utilizing
             the Loss of Load Expectation (“LOLE”) metric one (1) day in ten (10) years, or 0.1
             day per year. The tier determination, simulation, and allocation portions for the
             wind or solar resources ELCC Study shall be performed by the Transmission
             Provider on an annual basis for the Summer Season and Winter Season. The tier
             determination and allocation portions for the Electric Storage Resources ELCC
             Study, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources, shall be performed by
             the Transmission Provider on an annual basis. The simulation portion for the
             Electric Storage Resources ELCC Study, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric
             resources, shall be performed by the Transmission Provider for the Summer Season
             and Winter Season on a biennial basis, or more often as determined by the
             Transmission Provider, in accordance with Section 15.1(3) of this Attachment AA.
             The Transmission Provider, with input from the stakeholders, shall develop the
             inputs and assumptions to be used for ELCC study scope for each resource type.
             The ELCC Accredited Capacity as calculated in all studies and tiers shall be fully
       allocated to all resources. The results of the ELCC Study shall be valid for the
      upcoming Summer Season and Winter Season.
(2)   Set forth in this Section 15.1, wind resources, solar resources and Electric Storage
      Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources, will be assigned into
      two tiers. The Transmission Provider shall assign wind resources, solar resources,
      and Electric Storage Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources
      into tiers for each resource type as follows:
      (a)    Tier 1 – Designated Resources, resources associated with Firm Point-to-
             Point Transmission Service, and other resources with firm transmission
             service (with transmission service from those resources being accepted by
             the Transmission Provider by June 1 for the Summer Season and December
             1 for the Winter Season) for the designated amount.

      (b)    Tier 2 – Remaining resources that do not meet the requirements of Tier 1
             for the applicable season.

(3)   ELCC studies for each resource type studied pursuant to Section 15.1 of this
      Attachment AA will consist of a base case and one or more change cases utilizing,
      at least, the prior forty (40) historical weather years. The base case is defined as
      system load supplied by all other resource types in the SPP East Balancing
      Authority Area or the SPP West Balancing Authority Area that are not being
      evaluated.

      (a)    Wind and Solar Resources
             (i)     The wind ELCC Study base case will include load, conventional
                     resources, solar resources, hydroelectric resources, Energy Storage
                     Resources, and all other resources except for wind resources. The
                     solar ELCC Study base case will include load, conventional
                     resources, wind resources, hydroelectric resources, Energy Storage
                     Resources, and all other resources except for solar resources. The
                     first change case for the wind resources and solar resources will
                     include Tier 1 wind resources or Tier 1 solar resources, as
                     applicable. The second change case will include all wind or all solar
              resources. The base case and all change cases for the wind resources
             and solar resources will be analyzed by adding or removing the same
             amount of load in every hour of the assessment period until a total
             LOLE of 0.1 day per year is achieved across the totality of the
             historical weather years analyzed for the applicable season. The
             amount of load added or removed in each change case will be
             compared to the amount of load added in the base case to derive an
             ELCC megawatt (“MW”) for each change case across the totality of
             the historical weather years analyzed. The difference in total ELCC
             MW of the base case and the first change case is the ELCC MW
             assigned to Tier 1. The difference in total ELCC MW of the first
             change case and the second change case is the ELCC MW assigned
             to Tier 2.
(b)   Electric Storage Resources
      (i)    The Electric Storage Resource ELCC Study base case will include
             load, conventional resources, wind resources, solar resources,
             hydroelectric resources, and all other resources except for Electric
             Storage Resources that are not pumped storage hydroelectric
             resources. In the Electric Storage Resources ELCC Study, the
             storage resources will be scheduled to dispatch during high net load
             hours, which may cause the resource to be unavailable to meet a
             reliability need outside of the peak hours.

      (ii)   The simulation portion of the Electric Storage Resources ELCC
             Study shall analyze equipment with the durations listed below,
             defined by the equipment parameters. An ELCC curve based on
             penetration and accreditation percentage shall be established for
             each defined duration type. Each penetration amount will be
             analyzed by adding or removing the same amount of load in every
             hour of the assessment period until a total LOLE of 0.1 day per year
             is achieved across the totality of the historical weather years
             analyzed for the applicable season. The most recent ELCC curve for
                             each duration type shall be used for the allocation portion of the
                            Electric Storage Resource ELCC Study, as specified in Section 15.2
                            (2)(c)-(h) of this Attachment AA.

                            (a)     Eight hour duration equipment

                            (b)     Six hour duration equipment

                            (c)     Four hour duration equipment

15.2   Allocation to Individual ELCC Resources

       (1)   Wind and Solar Resources
             Once the total Accredited Capacity has been determined for each tier of wind and
             solar resource, each individual wind or solar resource will be assigned a percentage
             of the total Accredited Capacity of its corresponding tier. Tier 1 wind resources or
             solar resources will receive allocation, for each applicable season, based on the
             average production output of the individual resource during the top three percent
             (3%) Net Peak Load hours of the LRE in accordance with the SPP Planning
             Criteria. Full or partial forced events identified as Outside Management Control
             (“OMC”), as defined by NERC, that impact the production output of an individual
             resource included in Tier 1 shall be excluded from the determination of allocation
             of wind resources and solar resources in Tier 1. Individual resources of Tier 1 will
             then receive a pro-rata share of the total Accredited Capacity compared to the total
             historical average capacity value of all other wind resources or solar resources in
             the tier. Tier 2 wind resources and solar resources will receive allocation, for each
             applicable season, based on the average historical production output from the top
             three percent (3%) Net Peak Load hours of the applicable SPP Balancing Authority
             Area’s load in accordance with the SPP Planning Criteria. Full or partial forced
             events identified as OMC, as defined by NERC, that impact the production output
             of an individual resource included in Tier 2 shall be excluded from the
             determination of allocation of wind resources and solar resources in Tier 2.
             Individual resources of Tier 2 will then receive a pro-rata share of the total
       Accredited Capacity compared to the total historical average capacity value of all
      other wind resources and solar resources in Tier 2.

(2)   Electric Storage Resources
      (a)    The total penetration of Electric Storage Resources will dictate the
             percentage of accreditation that all Electric Storage Resources will receive
             based on each Tier and duration, regardless of location of the resource. The
             Transmission Provider shall perform the allocation process of the ELCC
             Study for Electric Storage Resources annually and shall utilize the most
             recent ELCC curves for each duration type in the process.

      (b)    Electric Storage Resources in Tier 1 will be prioritized before resources in
             Tier 2 when determining the Electric Storage Resource’s Accredited
             Capacity. All duration types will be prioritized in the order specified in
             Section 15.2(2)(c)-(h) of this Attachment AA within each tier. Resources
             that do not meet an hourly duration curve will be rounded down to the
             nearest hourly duration established. For an Electric Storage Resource to be
             allocated capacity with a higher duration within the same tier, the LRE shall
             notify the Transmission Provider and that resource must be de-rated to
             appropriate duration timeframe studied. Two hour Electric Storage
             Resources will have its Accredited Capacity determined with four hour
             duration Energy Storage Resources and shall receive no more than 50%
             accreditation.

      (c)    Eight hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 1 will be
             assigned the ELCC percentage of the eight hour duration curve for the total
             penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources identified as eight hour
             duration and Tier 1 for the applicable season;

      (d)    Six hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 1 will be
             assigned the ELCC percentage of the six hour duration curve for the total
             penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
             identified as:
       (i)     Tier 1 Eight hour duration; and

      (ii)    Tier 1 Six hour duration.

(e)   Four hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 1 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the four hour duration curve for the total
      penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
      identified as:

      (i)     Tier 1 Eight hour duration;

      (ii)    Tier 1 Six hour duration; and

      (iii)   Tier 1 Four hour duration

(f)   Eight hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 2 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the eight hour duration curve for the total
      penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
      identified as:

      (i)     All duration types of tier 1; and

      (ii)    Tier 2 Eight hour duration.

(g)   Six hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 2 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the six hour duration curve for the total
      penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
      identified as:

      (i)     All duration types of tier 1;

      (ii)    Tier 2 Eight hour duration; and

      (iii)   Tier 2 Six hour duration

(h)   Four hour duration Electric Storage Resources identified as Tier 2 will be
      assigned the ELCC percentage of the six hour duration curve for the total
      penetration amount of Electric Storage Resources for the applicable season
      identified as:
                       (i)     All duration types of tier 1;

                      (ii)    Tier 2 Eight hour duration;

                      (iii)   Tier 2 Six hour duration; and

                      (iv)    Tier 2 Four hour duration.

15.3   System ELCC Study

              An annual system ELCC Study shall be conducted by the Transmission Provider
       for the Summer Season and Winter Season separately for both the SPP East Balancing
       Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority Area to ensure the capacity value
       in the individual ELCC Studies is equivalent to the capacity value of the total system ELCC
       Study for the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area. The system ELCC Study base
       case will include load and all resources except for wind resources, solar resources, and
       Energy Storage Resources, excluding pumped storage hydroelectric resources. The system
       change case will include all resources and load. The difference in the total ELCC MW of
       the system base case and the ELCC MW of the system change case is the system ELCC
       MW. The capacity value determined in the system ELCC study shall be applied to the
       individual ELCC Studies for wind, solar, and Energy Storage Resource ELCC Studies on
       a pro rata basis according to the individual ELCC Studies.


15.4   Accredited Capacity Determination for Conventional Resources
       (1)    Each conventional resource’s Accredited Capacity shall be determined using a) the
              Net Generating Capability and b) the resource’s Conventional Resource
              Performance Adjustment for the applicable season. The resource’s Conventional
              Resource Performance Adjustment shall be determined using the resource’s a)
              EFORd for the applicable season and b) EFOF adjusted for Incremental Outage
              Impact of the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area for the applicable season.
              The individual resource’s adjusted EFOF is dependent upon the Incremental Outage
              Impact compared to the EFOF impact of all conventional resources of the
              applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area.              The Conventional Resource
              Performance Adjustment shall not exceed 100% for an individual resource. The
       Accredited Capacity and Conventional Resource Performance Adjustment
      calculations are as follows:

      Accredited Capacity
            =Net Generating Capability × (1 – Conventional Resource Performance
      Adjustment)
      Where:
      Conventional Resource Performance Adjustment
      = EFORd + (EFOF x Incremental Outage Impact / total system EFOF impact)
      Total system EFOF impact = Sum of [Net Generating Capability x EFOF] from
      all conventional resources of the applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area
(2)   The Transmission Provider shall determine a resource’s Conventional Resource
      Performance Adjustment in accordance with Section 15.4 of this Attachment AA
      and the SPP Business Practices. The full and partial forced outage events that
      occurred shall be used when determining the resource’s Conventional Resource
      Performance Adjustment. Authorized Outages (either full or partial) shall not be
      considered when calculating the resource’s Conventional Resource Performance
      Adjustment. The resulting EFORd and adjusted EFOF for an individual resource
      will be added together when determining the Conventional Resource Performance
      Adjustment for the applicable season.

      (a)      EFORd

               (i)    The EFORd shall be determined on an individual historical year
                      basis and averaged together considering all appropriate historical
                      years for the applicable season. A resource’s EFORd shall include
                      events occurring during the entire applicable season and exclude
                      OMC events, as defined by NERC.

               (ii)   The Transmission Provider shall calculate and post a weighted class
                      average EFORd for each applicable season. The weighted class
                      average EFORd shall be determined separately for the SPP East
                      Balancing Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority
                      Area. The resources shall be weighted against all other resources in
               the same class and in the same applicable SPP Balancing Authority
              Area for determining class average EFORd. The weighted class
              average EFORd shall be determined as follows:

              Sum of [Net Generating Capability x EFORd] from resources within
              the class / Sum of Net Generating Capability from resources within
              the class

(b)   EFOF

      (i)     The EFOF shall be determined on an individual historical year basis
              and averaged together considering all appropriate historical years
              for the applicable season. A resource’s EFOF shall include events
              occurring during the top three percent (3%) Adjusted Net Peak Load
              hours for the applicable season for each historical year. Certain
              OMC events, as defined in the SPP Business Practices, shall be
              included when determining the resource’s EFOF.

      (ii)    The Transmission Provider shall calculate and post a weighted class
              average EFOF for each applicable season. The weighted class
              average EFOF shall be determined separately for the SPP East
              Balancing Authority Area and the SPP West Balancing Authority
              Area. The resources shall be weighted against all other resources in
              the same class and in the same applicable SPP Balancing Authority
              Area for determining class average EFOF. The class average EFOF
              shall be calculated prior to the application of Incremental Outage
              Impact. The weighted class average EFOF shall be determined as
              follows:

              Sum of [Net Generating Capability x EFOF] from resources within
              the class / Sum of Net Generating Capability from resources within
              the class

      (iii)   The resource’s EFOF shall be further adjusted for Incremental
              Outage Impact. The Incremental Outage Impact shall be determined
                            by the Transmission Provider on a biennial basis in accordance with
                           the LOLE Study scope. The impact on the Base PRM between a
                           scenario including the modeled incremental correlated forced
                           outages and another scenario without the incremental correlated
                           forced outages shall be calculated and set as the Incremental Outage
                           Impact. The same amount of load shall be added or removed in every
                           hour of the assessment period until a resulting LOLE is achieved
                           across the totality of the historical weather years analyzed for the
                           applicable season and the resulting LOLE is equivalent between the
                           two scenarios. The Incremental Outage Impact shall be determined
                           separately for the SPP East Balancing Authority Area and the SPP
                           West Balancing Authority Area.

                    (iv)   In the event the Transmission Provider does not determine a
                           resource’s EFOF prior to the first season the resource is qualified
                           under this Attachment AA, the resource’s EFOF determined by the
                           entity shall not be adjusted for Incremental Outage Impact for the
                           first applicable season.

       (3)   Resources internal to the SPP Balancing Authority Areas qualified under this
             Attachment AA where historical performance data exists but is not provided for the
             applicable season shall have 100% EFORd and 100% EFOF applied to the
             applicable historical year and season in determining the resource’s Conventional
             Resource Performance Adjustment. Once a resource has been qualified, the
             Generator Owner, LRE, or Market Participant providing the historical data shall
             continually submit historical performance data to avoid a 100% EFORd and 100%
             EFOF applied to the applicable historical year and season.

15.5   Accredited Capacity Determination for Demand Response Resources and Reliability
       Registered Demand Response Programs
       (1)   Each Demand Response Resource’s and RRDRP’s Accredited Capacity shall be
             determined using the resource’s a) the Net Generating Capability and b) Demand
             Response Performance Adjustment for the applicable season. The resource’s
                Demand Response Performance Adjustment shall be determined using the
               resource’s a) actual metered load, b) expected Firm Service Level, c) Undeployed
               Availability, and d) Authorized Outages. The Accredited Capacity and Demand
               Response Performance Adjustment calculations for Demand Response Resources
               and RRDRPs are as follows:

                     𝐴𝑐𝑐𝑟𝑒𝑑𝑖𝑡𝑒𝑑 𝐶𝑎𝑝𝑎𝑐𝑖𝑡𝑦
                                   = 𝑁𝑒𝑡 𝐺𝑒𝑛𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝐶𝑎𝑝𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑦 𝑥 (100%
                                   ― 𝐷𝑒𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑅𝑒𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑒 𝑃𝑒𝑟𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝐴𝑑𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡)
      Where:
𝐷𝑒𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑑 𝑅𝑒𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑒 𝑃𝑒𝑟𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑛𝑐𝑒 𝐴𝑑𝑗𝑢𝑠𝑡𝑚𝑒𝑛𝑡


    (𝑎𝑐𝑡𝑢𝑎𝑙 𝑚𝑒𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑒𝑑 𝑙𝑜𝑎𝑑 ― 𝐹𝑖𝑟𝑚 𝑆𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑖𝑐𝑒 𝐿𝑒𝑣𝑒𝑙 ― 𝑈𝑛𝑑𝑒𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑦𝑒𝑑 𝐴𝑣𝑎𝑖𝑙𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑦 ― 𝐴𝑢𝑡ℎ𝑜𝑟𝑖𝑧𝑒𝑑 𝑂𝑢𝑡𝑎𝑔𝑒)
=                                                                                            𝑥
                                   𝑁𝑒𝑡 𝐺𝑒𝑛𝑒𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑛𝑔 𝐶𝑎𝑝𝑎𝑏𝑖𝑙𝑖𝑡𝑦


      (2)      The resource’s Demand Response Performance Adjustment shall be determined on
               an interval basis in accordance with Section 15.4 of this Attachment AA and the
               SPP Business Practices. Then, all applicable intervals will be averaged together in
               the applicable season to determine the resource’s Demand Response Performance
               Adjustment for the applicable season. The three (3) most recent years of historical
               information during the applicable season shall be used when determining the
               resource’s Demand Resource Performance Adjustment. The Demand Response
               Performance Adjustment shall not be less than 0% and shall not be greater than
               100%.

               (a)      In the event actual metered load is not submitted, the Demand Response
                        Performance Adjustment shall be set to 100% for the interval.
               (b)      In the event the actual metered load is less than or equal to the Firm Service
                        Level, the Undeployed Availability will not be considered, and the Demand
                        Response Performance Adjustment shall be set to zero for the interval.
               (c)      The Undeployed Availability shall only be considered during intervals
                        when the actual metered load is higher than the Firm Service Level and the
              resource has not been instructed to fully deploy by the Transmission
             Provider.
      (d)    Authorized Outages (either full or partial) shall be considered as a credit
             when calculating a Demand Response Resource’s Demand Response
             Performance Adjustment not exceeding the resource’s Net Generating
             Capability or remaining portion of Undeployed Availability in the interval.
             Authorized Outages shall not be considered as a credit when calculating the
             Demand Response Performance Adjustment for RRDRPs.


(3)   The intervals for consideration for the applicable Demand Response Resource and
      RRDRPs shall be determined based on the following:

      (a)    A Demand Response Resource’s Demand Response Performance
             Adjustment shall consider performance and availability for the applicable
             season as follows:
             (i)     availability and performance during the top three percent (3%)
                     Adjusted Net Peak Load hours of the applicable SPP Balancing
                     Authority Area;
             (ii)    availability and performance during all intervals when the
                     applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area is in conservative
                     operations advisory or any level of EEA Emergency Condition; and
             (iii)   performance during intervals when instructed to deploy by the
                     Transmission Provider.
      (b)    A Conservative Operations Demand Response Program’s Demand
             Response Performance Adjustment shall consider performance and
             availability for the applicable season as follows:
             (i)     availability and performance during all intervals when the
                     applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area is in conservative
                     operations advisory or any level of EEA Emergency Condition; and
             (ii)    performance during intervals when instructed to deploy by the
                     Transmission Provider.
       (c)    An Emergency Demand Response Program’s Demand Response
             Performance Adjustment shall consider the performance for the applicable
             season as follows:
             (i)    availability and performance during all intervals when the
                    applicable SPP Balancing Authority Area is in any level of EEA
                    Emergency Condition; and
             (ii)   performance during intervals when instructed to deploy by the
                    Transmission Provider.


(4)   The Transmission Provider shall determine a reliability-based Accredited Capacity
      limit for Emergency Demand Response Programs (“Emergency DR Limit”) and
      apply such limit in accordance with this Attachment AA and SPP Business
      Practices. The Emergency DR Limit shall be set in the SPP Planning Criteria and
      reviewed by the Transmission Provider on an as needed basis. Any change to the
      Emergency DR Limit shall be made no later than one year prior to the first
      applicable season.

(5)   An LRE’s total amount of qualified Demand Response Capacity for Emergency
      Demand Response Programs shall not exceed such LRE’s portion of the Emergency
      DR Limit for the applicable season.
